## Segmented-bar audit, round 2: five more screens, one adjacency fix carried over (her 2026-10-16 "continue the app-wide audit for other chip rows")
Surveyed the rest of the app beyond tongue/pulse/abdomen exam screens. Converted five clean matches; carried the Abdomen-style "name the sign on the extra" fix to one more screen that had the same defect; flagged one high-traffic but genuinely higher-risk family rather than guess at it blind.
- **Converted, reusing the existing `.ph-tng2-seg` CSS as-is (zero new styles, `.ph-ltr-qual`-based):** the Pulse exam's Referred signs row (`phVisitPulseHalfHtml`); the Treatment-plan-template "Clinical findings" chart editor's marks/body/coat/pulse-quality rows (`phTpFindingsHtml`, confirmed still LIVE — shown in the full-screen plan window's Clinical findings section and as the Visit-record Assessment fallback when a visit has no own findings, not dead code); the Guide page's "Tongue map" demo model's four rows (`phGdTngModelHtml`, confirmed a genuine demo with no record write-back — also added the `.ph-tng2-sep` divider its Shape·Thickness row was missing between its two categories, matching the pattern every other combined row already uses).
- **Converted with new, narrowly-scoped CSS (two chip families outside `.ph-ltr-qual`):** MSK's "Regions to examine" row (`phMskHeadHtml`/`phMskEmptyHtml`, class `.mk-chip`) and the Session grid's rhythm-preview row (`phTpSessionLadderHtml`, class `.ph-tpg-p3.rh`). Both keep their OWN category colour on pick (MSK blue `--ph-msk`, herb-deep) — the new CSS only adds the structural joining (flatten corners, shared divider, no individual pill border), it deliberately does NOT redefine `.on`'s background. For `.mk-chip` this needed the extra `.ph-msk` ancestor qualifier in the selector (`#pharmacyPage .ph-msk .ph-tng2-seg .mk-chip`) to reliably out-rank the existing same-specificity `.ph-msk .mk-chip` base rule regardless of source order — ran the same "would this actually win" specificity check the earlier rounds did, rather than assuming a `.ph-tng2-seg` ancestor alone would be enough (it wasn't, for this one: 2 classes vs 2 classes is a tie, and the original rule sits later in the file).
- **Carried the Abdomen adjacency fix to `phRenReviewChartHtml`** (the Ren tab's separate "dated review" tongue chart editor): its Coat quality, Marks, and the marks half of Shape·Moist all had the identical defect Abdomen had — a zone tag + "where"/"tap the drawing" button printed right after each ticked sign with no sign name on either, adjacency the only thing linking them. Same fix: `pick()` now takes the sign's own label and prints it on both the zone tag and the button ("Red spots — where", "**Red spots** left ✕"); each row's chips now join into `.ph-tng2-seg` while the extras move to a `.ph-tng2-extras` strip underneath (same CSS, same pattern as Abdomen, nothing new). `coatRow` and `devRow` were pulled into named variables (previously inline in the template) purely so they could be `seg2()`-wrapped the same way as everything else in the function — no behaviour change.
- **Looked at and deliberately NOT converted, disclosed rather than guessed:** the Cycle day log's Flow/Pain/Clots/Discharge/LH/PMS chip rows (`phCycleSelectChips`, class `.ph-ck-chip`/`.ph-ck-chips`) are structurally a clean, textbook match for the rule — including per-option colour already wired for Flow (flow-heavy/med/light/spot) and LH (lh-pos) — and are very high traffic (every patient, every day logged). **Not converted this round**: `.ph-ck-chip` is reused across many OTHER, unrelated surfaces (Communications message chips, the acu watch/mucus/lifestyle rows, the cycle-day finder, filters) with roughly a dozen different nested-context CSS overrides already layered on top of it (`.cp-card .cp-log.ph-cycle-signpop`, `.cp-box`, `.cp-foot`, `.ph-cyc-fd`, phone-specific rules, several animation/transition exceptions) — each independently tuned over many earlier, separately-confirmed builds. A scoped `.ph-tng2-seg` override risks either losing a specificity fight against one of those nested rules (producing a double-border look, chips keeping their own pill shape inside the "joined" bar) or, if given enough specificity to win everywhere, flattening sizing/spacing in a context it was never tuned for — and this file has no live render available to verify a change this deep against, unlike the simpler single-definition classes converted above. Flagging for her explicit go-ahead (or a dedicated pass with real-device verification) rather than attempting it blind on her most-used page.
- Also confirmed, one-line each, as genuinely out of scope (not flagged further): `phVisitHmChips` (Pulse Hammer exam quality stamps — still a dense many-position grid, the rule's own "long list" exception); `phVisitHmModsHtml`'s degree+change row (mixes a pick-one degree scale with an unrelated "△ change" action chip in one row — excluded for mixing categories/actions, not an adjacency problem); `phHxConstitPulseHtml`'s "other quality" stamp row (a brush/tool palette — tap a stamp, then tap grid cells to place it, with a "more (N)" fold and "✕ erase" mixed in, not a standing pick/tick row); `phCyclePopHtml`'s older Flow/Pain chips (legacy box, reachable only via Period history's own ✎ edit, superseded by `phCycleSignPopHtml`); MSK's pain "feel" word tags (her own separately confirmed design, 2026-10-14 Option C — a tap-to-open tool palette for a Detail box, not a pick/tick row); Appointments' day-of-week chips (explicitly exempted by the TAPPABLE THINGS rule itself — "Mon–Sun toggles" stay chips); Came in for's quick-pick chips (already migrated to the separate `.ph-pfw-opt` pattern, 2026-10-15).
- **NOT exercised** (same sandbox limitation as every round of this audit): a real signed-in render, her phone, a real tap. Verified by reading each edited function, its call sites, and the CSS selectors/specificity it now depends on.

## Timeline promoted to its own rail step; approximate (month/year) dates on Schedule (her 2026-10-16, build 20261016-1002000, committed on `session-a` — LIVE on main (audited 2026-10-18: origin/main has since advanced past this build))
Two asks in one window: (1) a screenshot of the patient rail (numbered steps, Timeline buried as "0 of 9" under Treatment Care Plan) — "i need a menstrual/ivf/cycle step/section purely for tracking that"; (2) a screenshot of a Timeline Schedule form ("Egg collection", date box, Note, Save/Cancel) — "give option to give approximate date e.g. month/year". Three clarifying questions on the first ask, all three "Recommended" picks taken: Timeline promoted to its own step (not a new page, not folded into Cycle); shown only on IVF / Natural fertility / Pregnancy plans (`phTlKindOf` truthy); positioned right after Fang Bing Ren, before Treatment Care Plan.
- **Timeline step (`presFlowSteps`/`presFlowRailHtml`/`presStageNextBtnHtml`/`presVisitNext`/`presTpMainSections`):** a `tlKind`/`tlDone` computation feeds a conditional `{id:"timeline", ...}` entry spliced into the `steps` array between Fang Bing Ren's patterns sub-row and the Treatment Care Plan step, with `n:` now derived via `.map((s,i)=>({...s,n:i+1}))` instead of hardcoded, so patients without a timeline (non-fertility plans) keep clean 1-6 numbering. "Done" = nothing overdue on the live `phTlModel` (never stored, same as every other step's done-state). Included in the Next-button order array and in `presVisitNext`'s walk on BOTH first and return visits (not gated on return-visit status — it's ongoing tracking, not a one-glance item). The old "Phases"/"Timeline" two-item `planSubs` row under Treatment Care Plan is gone (`planSubs: []`); the Timeline rail page itself (`presTpMainSections`) just moved earlier in the section order to match.
  - **Real rendering bug found and fixed along the way, not a user report:** `presFlowRailHtml`'s `inner` template hardcodes a `stepHtml()` call per named step variable rather than generically iterating `f.steps` — a new step added only to the `steps` array had correct numbering but never actually rendered. Added `const tlStep = f.steps.find(s => s.id === "timeline")` (the file's own "look up by id, never position" convention) and inserted `${tlStep ? stepHtml(tlStep) : ""}` into `inner` at the right spot. Caught by live DOM testing (a `.ph-flow-step` query came up one short), not by reading the code.
  - Verified live in the sandbox (synthetic IVF-plan patient): Timeline button appears at position 4 with the right label/caption/done-state; artificially scheduling an overdue item flips `tlDone` false→true as designed; a non-fertility plan (`phTpNewPlan` with no matching template) correctly shows no Timeline step and clean 1-6 numbering with no leftover artifacts.
- **Approximate date on the Schedule form only** (`phTlSchedFormHtml`, the click-handler block for `data-tl-sch-open`/`data-tl-sd-approx`/`data-tl-sch-save`/cancel/clear, `phTlModel`'s `defs.forEach` loop, five display call sites): a "Month/year only" checkbox (`data-tl-sd-approx`) swaps `<input type="date">` for `<input type="month">`; a view-state draft (`phTlUi.schDraft`) carries whatever she's already typed (date↔month, converted; the note) across the swap so toggling never discards her in-progress input. **Storage:** an approximate schedule is the 1st of that month in the existing `YYYY-MM-DD` key shape, plus a new `approx: true` flag — `phTlOkDate`'s regex and every other date-consuming path are untouched by design. **Display:** `phTlSchedTxt(sched)` branches on `.approx` to show "Sep 2026" instead of a specific day, read by `phTlTip`, `phTlDoneCellHtml`'s Reschedule view, `phTlTableHtml`'s "When" column, `phPtnTip` (the partner-link tooltip) and the detail-panel branch — one function, five call sites, never five separate formatters.
  - Verified live end-to-end in the sandbox (synthetic IVF-plan patient, real DOM events — `.click()` on the checkbox, not a property poke, so the delegated click handler actually fires): checkbox toggle swaps date↔month inputs correctly; typing a month + note and Save writes `{date:"2026-09-01", note, approx:true, at}`; the rendered Timeline shows "Sep 2026" (not a day) and correctly reads "Overdue" once that month has passed, same rule as any other missed planned date; reopening Reschedule pre-fills the checkbox checked, the month value, and the note; toggling the checkbox back off converts the stored month back to a date value (`2026-09-01`) with the note intact, confirming the draft-carrying logic works in both directions; saving as an exact date afterward correctly writes `approx:false`.
- **Disclosed scope decision:** the "Mark done" form was NOT touched or given the same month/year option — her ask was specifically about the Schedule form (a future date she doesn't know exactly), not Mark done (a past event, which should usually have a known date).
- Synthetic test patient and script item created for this round's live testing were deleted from the sandbox after verification, mirroring the cleanup convention from the Timeline-step round.

## Musculoskeletal page: "+ Pain map" door missing on Pregnancy/fertility plans (her 2026-10-16 "why can't i add info for pain map?", build 20261016-1003000, committed on `session-a` — LIVE on main (audited 2026-10-18: origin/main has since advanced past this build))
Her screenshot of the Musculoskeletal Assessments page for a Pregnancy-plan patient: Pain intake + Pain score + Examination sections, but no "Where it hurts" pain map and no "+ Pain map" button anywhere — she had no way to log where a pregnancy-related pain (back, pelvis, SIJ, etc.) actually was.
- **Root cause** (`phPainMapHtml`): the empty-state branch deliberately returns `""` (no door at all) when the plan is "cyclish" (`PH_TP_CYCLE_TEMPLATES` or `templateName === "Pregnancy"`) and nothing is on file yet — a documented, correct choice for the Treatment Care Plan tile and Patient details, where pain isn't necessarily the point of a fertility/pregnancy visit. But the Musculoskeletal Assessments page (`phMskPageHtml` → `phMskPainCardHtml` → `presRvPainHtml` → `phPainMapHtml`) reuses the exact same function, so the same suppression silently hid the door on the ONE page whose whole purpose is pain tracking regardless of plan (her own 2026-10-11 "always visible" law) — and pregnancy-related MSK pain is common and clinically worth logging.
- **Fix:** the door still suppresses on a cyclish plan everywhere EXCEPT while `phPmScoreCtx === plan.id` — a flag already set only for the duration of `phMskPainCardHtml`'s own call, so no new state or parameter was needed. The Care Plan tile and Patient details keep their existing quiet behaviour unchanged; only the Musculoskeletal page now offers the door on a Pregnancy/fertility plan with nothing logged yet.
- Verified live in the sandbox (synthetic Pregnancy-plan patient, no pain data, real DOM clicks through the real delegated handlers): the "+ Pain map" door renders on the Musculoskeletal page where it was previously absent; clicking it opens the real region picker (Head & neck / Shoulder & arm / Back / Chest & abdomen / Hip & leg tabs); picking "Sacroiliac joint" under Back writes a real pain entry (`plan.painMap`) and the page repaints to show the actual "Where it hurts" figure with the logged spot, confirming the full add-a-pain flow works end to end. Synthetic patient and script item deleted from the sandbox after verification.
- **Not exercised:** a real patient, her phone, confirming the Care Plan tile and Patient-details pages are still unaffected on a real render (read from source only — their call sites don't set `phPmScoreCtx`, so the logic change cannot reach them, but not independently clicked through).

## Patient Details ↔ Timeline linkage: a one-line next-milestone summary, and Open routes straight to it (her 2026-10-16 screenshot of Zoie Wynn's "ONE box" card + "i want to audit and make sure that the patient details page links with timeline page. where is the embryo transfer and egg collection tracking?", build 20261016-1005000, committed on `session-a` — LIVE on main (audited 2026-10-18: origin/main has since advanced past this build))
Audit: the Patient Details plan band's "Open" button always landed on the Care Plan tab, never Timeline, even for a Pregnancy/Natural fertility/IVF Protocol/Men's fertility plan that HAS a Timeline — so egg collection and embryo transfer dates were reachable only by opening the plan then tapping into its own Timeline sub-page, never from Patient Details directly. Asked her how to close the gap via two offered fixes; she picked **both**.
- **A Timeline line on the card** (`phPfTlLineHtml(rec, name, plan)`, new, placed right after `phTlSideHtml` since it reads the exact same `phTlModel`): one tappable Row (`.ph-pf-tlline`, inserted into `presPfPlanTileHtml` between `${pips}` and `${earlierHtml}`) showing the next OPEN (not-done) milestone — "Timeline  Partner semen analysis  *Not planned*" — sorted by `lo` (Pregnancy, week-based) or `dLo` (every other kind, date-based). Blank (`return ""`) when the plan has no Timeline (`phTlKindOf` falsy) or every item is already done — never a second description of the same dates the Timeline page itself already renders; `phTlWhenText(kind, it)` was extracted as a shared helper out of `phTlSideHtml`'s own inline closure so both read identically, never two wordings of the same date.
- **Open routes to Timeline when one exists:** `presPfPlanTileHtml` adds `data-pf-plan-tab="timeline"` to the band's own Open button (never the "Earlier" finished-plan buttons — reviewing a completed plan should still land on Care Plan, not Timeline); the `data-pf-plan-open` click handler reads that attribute and passes it through as a new third argument to `presTpInlineOpen(name, planId, tab)`, which sets `presTpMainTab = tab || null` instead of always `null`. A plan with no Timeline keeps the old behaviour exactly (no attribute, no third argument, lands on Care Plan as before).
- **CSS:** `.ph-pf-tlline` is a Row per the TAPPABLE THINGS five-shape rule (a whole-row tap target on a faint surface, not a Chip or Button — it both displays a fact and opens something on tap), matching the card's existing density (`--ph-white` background, 9px radius, `--fs-12-5`, `--ph-soft` text, `--ph-faint` for the `<em>` date, hover tints `--ph-herb-tint`). An `.over` modifier (an overdue milestone) reuses the TIMELINE WIDGET'S OWN overdue tokens (`--ph-low-tint`/`--ph-low-deep`, the same ones `.ph-tlx-st.over`/`.ph-tlx-s.over` already use) — caught and corrected a first draft that invented non-existent `--ph-warn-tint`/`--ph-warn-deep` tokens before committing, by rendering the `.over` state live and finding it painted transparent/unstyled.
- Verified live in the sandbox (synthetic IVF-plan patient, real function calls — `phPfTlLineHtml`, `presPfPlanTileHtml`, `presTpInlineOpen` — through the real `phPatientPeek`/`phTpFindPlan` data path, not a hand-typed stand-in): the Timeline line renders with the real next-open-item text and date wording; the Open button carries `data-pf-plan-tab="timeline"` only when the plan has a Timeline (confirmed both true for IVF Protocol and false for a plain Neck & shoulder plan); `presTpInlineOpen("name","planZZ1","timeline")` correctly sets `presTpMainTab` to `"timeline"`; the rendered `.ph-pf-tlline` computed style matches the card (white bg, 9px radius, 12.5px text) and the `.over` modifier, after the token fix, renders the correct amber tint/text. Synthetic patients removed from the sandbox after verification.
- **Not exercised:** a real patient, her phone, a real tap-through (only direct function calls and a static-markup render were tested — no live click dispatched through the real `data-pf-plan-open` delegated handler on a rendered profile page).

## Cycle page: the Day log and Usual period cards share one group system (her 2026-10-16, screenshots of both cards + "these two essential measure same chips - redesign the chips to group them and make the page less redundant. show mock", build 20261016-1007000, committed on `session-a` — LIVE on main (audited 2026-10-18: origin/main has since advanced past this build))
Mock `cycle-chips-grouped-mock-2026-10-16.html` (sent as an image before asking, per her standing "open visuals before asking" rule), plus a second comparison panel proving a joined bar breaks for a tick-several row (a picked chip that wraps alone stretches full-width) vs. loose chips, which don't. Two rounds of `AskUserQuestion` (4 each, all 8 answers **Recommended**): shared group headers Bleeding / Discomfort / Signs & mood, same order on both cards; the Day log's LH/Sex/Other-twinge trio keeps its own 4th "Other signs" group (nothing to match on Usual); PMS (and any tick-several row) stays loose chips, never a joined bar; Day log's Pain stays two rows (0-10 slider + Pain type); BBT gets its own small group after Bleeding; scope = the full Cycle page's two cards only, not the smaller popovers elsewhere; long bars wrap to a second line on a narrow card, never scroll; both cards built in one pass.
- **Usual period** (`PH_PFW_SETS.period.qs`, `presPfwSetHtml`): each question now carries an opt-in `grp` field ("Bleeding"/"Discomfort"/"Signs & mood"); the array was reordered so same-group questions sit consecutively (len→flow→col→clot, then pain→cm, then limbs→pms — was len→flow→pain→cm→clot→col→limbs→pms). `presPfwSetHtml` walks `set.qs` and prints a `.ph-pfw-grphd` header whenever `q.grp` changes from the previous row; a question with no `grp` (every OTHER set — meno/men/pain) renders exactly as before, no headers, fully backward compatible.
- **Day log** (`phCycleSignPopHtml`'s `opts.flat` branch — the Cycle page's own "All signs" full card; confirmed via live render this is the ONLY branch her screenshot came from): rows reordered and grouped the same way — Bleeding (Flow, Colour, Clots) → BBT (its own group, `phCycBbtRowHtml`'s flat row now carries `full` so it doesn't pair oddly with an unrelated field) → Discomfort (Pain slider, Pain type, Discharge) → Signs & mood (PMS, unchanged loose chips) → Other signs (LH, Sex, Ovulation twinge) → Note. Group headers reuse the SAME `.ph-pfw-grphd` class as Usual period (one shared visual language, not a second near-duplicate style), printed via a local `grphd()` helper.

## Fertility timeline: real sync with IVF history (her 2026-10-16 screenshot + "sync timeline with ivf history, especially for blood test, transfer, egg collection etc. sync it and make it cohesive", build 20261016-1010000, committed on `session-a` — LIVE on main (audited 2026-10-18: origin/main has since advanced past this build))
Her screenshot (IVF Protocol Timeline, Checklist view): Baseline scan and bloods, Stimulation scans, Egg collection, Fertilisation report, Embryo transfer and Heartbeat scan ALL showed "Not planned" with only manual Schedule/Mark-done — except Pregnancy blood test, which correctly showed "Done 16 Oct · Positive blood · hCG 205". Investigated rather than guessed: this was a real bug, not a missing feature or a quirk of her data.
- **Root cause (`phIvfLinkedCollection`):** the Timeline only ever reads an IVF-history round that carries `linkedPlanId`/`linkedRound` — but those fields are ONLY ever stamped by the plan's own Cycle-page date widget (`phIvfLinkedCollectionWritable`, reached from `data-ivfd-mark`). A round logged the ORDINARY way — IVF history's own "+ Egg collection"/"+ Transfer" buttons, which is how she actually logs a round — never gets linked, so `base`/`stim` (scans, via `phIvfScanList`), `opu` (egg collection), `et` (embryo transfer), and anything derived from them (`fert`, `beta`'s date filter, `hb`'s estimate window) all read nothing. The one item that DID work, `beta` (pregnancy blood test), uses a separate reader (`phTlPregTestRead`) with no link check at all — the same "just read her latest round" pattern already used for a partner's view of her timeline (`phTlPtnData`).
- **Fix, scoped to the read side only (never touches the write-path widget, which is unchanged and still correct):** `phIvfLinkedCollection` now falls back to the patient's own latest NOT-explicitly-linked round (excluding a `freeze`-kind round, same exclusion `phTlPtnData`'s precedent already uses) whenever nothing is explicitly linked to this exact plan+round — an explicitly linked round still always wins, so a patient on her SECOND IVF attempt (a new plan, an old already-linked round from the first attempt) is never misattributed. Verified live: an old round linked to nothing and a properly-linked round present together correctly surface the LINKED one, not the fallback.
- **Fertilisation report wired for the first time:** it previously only ever showed an estimated "retrieval + 1 day" with no way to mark it Done from real data, even though the round already captures `fertilised`/`day3`/`blastocysts` (the same fields the round's own conversion-funnel display reads). Now shows "7 fertilised · 6 on day 3 · 4 blastocysts" automatically once those numbers are on the round, confirmed (not estimated) the same way Egg collection's eggs-count already was.
- **Heartbeat scan is a genuine data gap, not fixed here, disclosed:** nothing in IVF history captures a heartbeat-scan date or result at all (scans only cover pre-transfer monitoring — follicle sizes, lining, hormone levels). With the link fixed it now at least shows the right ESTIMATED window (transfer + 30 days, "~15 Nov") instead of nothing, but marking it Done still needs a manual tap — there is no field anywhere to read a real result from. Adding one is new schema work, not asked for here.
- **Not duplicated, not touched:** the Cycle-page date widget (`phIvfLinkedCollectionWritable`) is completely unchanged — it still always creates/targets a properly linked round when she types a date there. A patient who logs a round through IVF history and THEN also types a date through the widget could end up with two rounds (the fallback-matched one and a newly linked one) — a pre-existing risk this fix doesn't introduce or worsen, since the widget never looked at unlinked rounds either way; flagged rather than silently "fixed" with a riskier write-side auto-link.
- Verified live via a scratch local server + the Browser pane, real `phTlModel` calls (not a hand-typed stand-in): a synthetic IVF-plan patient with a single UNLINKED round (12 eggs, 9 mature, 7 fertilised, 6 on day 3, 4 blastocysts, 2 PGT-normal, 2 scans, a positive-result transfer) now shows every item Done with real data — base/stim from the real scan readings, opu "12 eggs", fert "7 fertilised · 6 on day 3 · 4 blastocysts", et the real transfer date, beta unchanged, hb showing the correct estimated window. A second check (an old unlinked round + a properly linked round both present) confirmed the linked round still wins. No new console errors.
- **Not exercised:** a real patient, her phone, a real tap through the rendered Timeline page (only direct `phTlModel` calls were run).

- Verified live via a scratch local server + the Browser pane, synthetic photo records injected straight into `phRenPhotoCache` (today natural/sublingual/flash, a week-ago natural/sublingual — no flash a week ago, deliberately, to exercise the "no earlier photo" empty state) and real calls to `phTngCmpPick`/`phTngCmpHtml` (not a hand-typed stand-in): `phTngCmpPick(name,"t",...)` correctly excludes flash and sublingual from both today's and last's picks; `"sub"` and `"flash"` each correctly isolate their own shot; the flash kind's `last` correctly comes back `null` and its fixed section renders "No earlier photo on file" + the disclosed note; the TOP panel's rendered HTML contains no "Under" text under `kind:"t"` and no "Tongue body"/More-fold button under `kind:"sub"`, while Under IS present under `"sub"`; exactly two `.ph-tc-sec` blocks render (Sublingual, Flash) with real, non-overlapping `getBoundingClientRect()`s (845×327 each) once injected into the real `#pharmacyPage` DOM with the real stylesheet applied. Full page boot showed no new console errors (the one present is the known offline-sandbox external-script-fetch limitation, unrelated).

## IVF history redesign: the full 6-point rebuild (her 2026-10-16, mock `ivf-redesign-mock-2026-10-16.html`, "Yes, build all of it"; six commits on `session-a` — all LIVE on main (confirmed ancestors of origin/main as of the 2026-10-18 audit))
A full UX redesign of IVF-history recording, mocked and approved whole, then built in six passes (the commit messages number them 1/6-3/6 against the ORIGINAL plan order below, which does not line up 1:1 with the numbering inside each message — read this entry, not the numbers in `git log`, for which commit is which point).
1. **The round card stays open once opened** (`rec.ivfHistOpen`/`rec.ivfOpenIds`), persisting across visits — commit `fbcef68`.
2. **One merged outcome field** (replacing two previously unsynced mechanisms) — commit `fbcef68`.
3. **Starting a transfer shows/lets her change which round it attaches to** (ambiguous-pick flagging + one-tap reattachment) — commit `fbcef68`.
4. **Quick-log by moment** (`fbcef68`'s sibling, commit `f8b0e41`): four single-purpose quick forms (Scan check-in / Retrieval day / Transfer day / Results call) on the IVF history card instead of the full round-card funnel, today's due moment auto-detected and highlighted (`phIvfQuickDue`, priority order results > transfer > retrieval > scan). Each writes the exact same round/transfer/scan shape the existing "+ Egg collection"/"+ Transfer" doors use — a faster door onto the one record, never a second one. Added an honest new `folTotal` field (a combined follicle count, never folded into the one-sided `folR`, which would misreport it) threaded through every scan display and write path.
5. **Scan bloods merged into the shared Blood-tests store** (commit `1dfa932`): an IVF monitoring scan's e2/lh/p4/fsh/amh are the same markers `PH_BLD_MARKERS` and the Natural-fertility Timeline's own "Day 2-3 hormones"/AMH items already track. `phBldList` now merges them in on every READ (`phIvfScanBldRows`) rather than copying them into a second stored record, so editing the scan stays the one edit. hCG was deliberately left out — no catalog entry, rare on a monitoring scan, and a pregnancy hCG already has its own correct home on the transfer (`t.pregHcg`). The Blood-tests table shows a merged column read-only (no edit/delete there — the scan itself is the one place to change it); typical-range flags (none fire — cycle hormones carry no fixed range) and the 12-month staleness rule both apply normally. Verified this makes the Timeline's AMH/Day-2-3-hormones items resolve from real scan data with no separate entry, and that it doesn't touch Fang Bing Ren's existing blood ticks (uric acid, etc. — none of the merged markers are wired to a sign).
6. **A cross-patient "today's IVF work" list** (commit `67e2535`): **disclosed finding, not a silent reinterpretation** — the plan's own wording ("behind Appointments' existing 'Cycle & IVF' lens chip") assumed a UI entry point that turned out to be stale: `phApptLensHit`'s `"cycle"` branch is still live code, but the lens-chip ROW it belonged to was superseded by later redesigns (the Appointments List rebuild, the 2026-10-15 dead-code sweep removing `PH_APPTCAL_LENSES`) and nothing in the current app still sets `phApptCalLens` to `"cycle"`/`"herbs"`/`"new"`/`"home"` — only `"all"` and `"prac:<name>"` (the practitioner row) remain reachable. Rather than resurrect a chip for a DIFFERENT, broader filter ("on a cycle-tracking plan" vs. "has IVF action due today"), this builds the actual deliverable directly: a "Today's IVF work" band on the Appointments page (`phIvfTodayWorkBandHtml`, right under the practitioner chip row) scanning EVERY patient on file (`phIvfTodayWorkRows`, not just today's bookings — monitoring often happens at the fertility clinic with no LCM appointment that day) through `phIvfQuickDue`, so this list and the quick-log bar can never disagree about what's due. No fold, no new page — hidden entirely when nothing's due anywhere, same posture as the existing "Herbs to prepare today" list.
- Every point sandbox-verified through real DOM click/change-event dispatch (not direct function calls) against synthetic patients, deleted after each verification pass: all four quick-log moments write their exact fields; the due-priority order resolves correctly when several moments could apply at once; the "no round yet"/"no transfer awaiting" fallback messages render; the quick bar and the IVF-today band both stay hidden for a patient/practice with nothing due; the merged blood row renders correctly alongside a real manual blood test with correct sort/flagging/staleness; the Appointments band's patient-name link opens the real profile; no new console errors anywhere.
- **Git housekeeping, disclosed:** built across two sessions on one shared working tree, each commit isolated to its own hunks via `git apply --cached` + a no-paths `git commit` (never `git add -A`/`git commit -- <paths>`) specifically because a concurrent session was mid-edit on `index.html` at the same time — confirmed before every commit that nothing of theirs was swept in. Both version markers (`sw.js` `CACHE_VERSION`, the `<meta name="lcm-build">` stamp) were bumped together on every one of the six commits.
- **Not exercised anywhere in this build:** a real patient, her phone, a real screenshot (the sandbox's sign-in overlay covers the DOM even though the real render and every event dispatch work correctly through direct access — a known, previously-documented limitation of this environment).

- **Multi-select, Colour and Shape (her ask 2):** **Shape was already multi-select** (`t.shape` is an array via `phTng2Toggle`'s existing branch) — nothing to change there; her screenshot likely read it as single-pick only because a joined segmented bar looks the same whether it holds one pick or several (that's the point of the 2026-10-15 bar rule). **Colour was genuinely single-pick**, now widened: `tng.colour` stays the PRIMARY value — the exact same bare string every existing reader already expects (the chart SVG body colour, the "Reads as" summary, the two Fang Bing Ren chart-word readers `phFbrTng2Words` and `phPatClues`' own tongue flag reader) — and a new `tng.colourMore[]` holds any FURTHER colours ticked. This is the Pulse chart's own "several qualities in one cell" `base + more[]` pattern (her 2026-10-13 build), reused rather than the `coatQual`/`marks` keyed-object shape, because it lets every existing single-string reader keep working untouched instead of needing a rewrite. `phTng2Toggle`'s new `colour` branch: tapping an unticked chip sets it as primary if none is set, else pushes it onto `colourMore`; tapping the primary again untick it and promotes the next `colourMore` entry (if any); tapping a ticked secondary removes just that one. `phTng2Read` normalises `colourMore` to an array and de-dupes/strips anything matching the primary (defensive, in case of a bad write). `phTng2Empty` and `phTng2Summary` (the "Reads as" sentence) both read `colourMore` too. **Old saved data (a bare string, no `colourMore` key) reads correctly with no migration** — `Object.assign` over `phTng2Blank()`'s new `colourMore: []` default handles it. Changed in the shared `phTng2*` functions so the standalone Examine page (`phVisitTongueHtml`'s `colourRow`) picks up the same multi-select behaviour automatically (her own "both screens should behave consistently" allowance) — its layout was not touched, only the "on" check for the colour chip (`t.colour === k || t.colourMore.includes(k)`), same one-line fix as the viewer's own `colour` row. **Coat thickness/colour deliberately left single-pick** — a disclosed, smaller-surface scope cut (the task's own fallback), since Coat wasn't asked about as explicitly as Colour/Shape and widening it would mean auditing a second set of readers for no confirmed need yet.
- **Purple and Blue (her ask 3):** **"Purple" already existed** in `PH_TNG_COLOURS` since the original detailed-tongue-chart build (`8f7e177`) — it was not missing, and was already wired to the Ren sign `tongue_purple` ("Tongue: dark or purple") via `PH_TNG_FBR_MAP` (`tongue_purple: [["colour","purple"]]`) and `PH_FBR_CHART_PREFILL` (`words: ["purple","dusky"]`) — those were simply dormant pending nothing, since the chip itself was already rendering on this exact screen before this session started. Nothing needed building for purple beyond what the multi-select change above already gives it (it can now sit alongside another ticked colour). **"Blue" is new** — added to `PH_TNG_COLOURS` with its own swatch hex (`#5C7CBB`), picked up automatically by every reader that was widened for multi-select above (chip row, chart-word extraction, summary). **Left OFF the Fang Bing Ren wiring on purpose**: the existing `tongue_purple` sign's own wording says "dark or purple," not "blue" — tying a blue tick to it would be inventing a clinical association she hasn't confirmed, not reusing an existing one (per the task's own instruction to disclose rather than invent). Disclosed gap, hers to extend if she wants a blue-tongue sign built.
- **Centre crack (her ask 4):** added to the shared `PH_TNG_MARKS` table (`["crackC", "centre crack"]`, between `crackH` and `teeth`) — both consumers that read this one array pick it up with no separate wiring: the chip row (`phRenTngSecHtml`, `phVisitTongueHtml`, the dated-review/template-findings editors) and the typed-circle tool's type picker (`phRenMarkTypePlaceHtml`). Follows the exact same pattern as `crack`/`crackH`, which also carry no Fang Bing Ren sign — so centre crack ticks nothing there either, consistent rather than a new precedent. Also added a small SVG drawing for it (`crackC`, a single fixed line down the tongue's centre, same "fixed drawing, not per-region" shape as `twolines`) so the optional "Drawing" toggle view stays visually complete — this one extra touch wasn't strictly asked for but costs one line and avoids a silently-missing glyph next to its siblings.
- **Verified:** a standalone Node-free logic harness (the real `phTng2Blank`/`Toggle`/`Read`/`Empty`/`Summary`/`phFbrTng2Words` bodies, copied verbatim and run inside headless Edge via `--dump-dom`, since this folder's 5-dev-server cap was already held by other concurrent chats and `preview_start` refused a 6th) confirmed, all passing: (a) an old bare-string record (`{colour:"red", shape:["swollen"]}`) still reads as `colour:"red"`, is not reported empty, and its summary is unchanged; (b) ticking a 2nd and 3rd colour builds `colourMore` correctly, untick-the-primary promotes the next tick, untick-the-last clears everything back to a genuinely empty record; (c) the summary sentence lists every ticked colour ("pale, blue, swollen"); (d) `phFbrTng2Words` emits BOTH the primary and a secondary colour, so the dormant `tongue_purple` prefill still fires even when purple is ticked as someone's *second* colour, not their first; (e) `blue` and `crackC`/"centre crack" exist as distinct, correctly-labelled entries, and shape's pre-existing multi-select is unaffected. Confirmed by direct code reading (not live-rendered) that `PH_TNG_MARKS` is the one array both the chip row and `phRenMarkTypePlaceHtml` consume, so centre crack reaches both automatically. **Not exercised: a live signed-in render of the viewer itself (chip markup, 1280/375px layout, a real click through the delegated handler, console-error sweep)** — this folder's dev-server slots were full from other chats' sessions throughout, and loading `index.html` directly via `file://` in headless Edge crashed ("Multiple targets are not supported in headless mode"), a known Chromium headless limitation this file hasn't hit before; recommend a quick visual check on her own machine or a later session with a free server slot before pushing. ## Patient details avatar: choose from her existing photos, not just a fresh capture (synth22 batch, Workstream D, 2026-10-16; committed on `session-a` — LIVE on main (audited 2026-10-18: origin/main has since advanced past this build))
Her ask, verbatim: "Give option to choose profile picture from photos table." Scope = the Patient details Identity card's avatar + camera-badge mechanism only. Did NOT touch Find the Ren (`3d36675`), the Tongue photo viewer (`77b08c7`) or the Pulse "Normal range" toggle (`398dc29`) — confirmed by reading the diff, which only touches `.ph-pf-avatar*`/`.ph-pfav-*` CSS, the `data-pf-avatar-add` click branch, and the new `phPfAvatar*` functions.
- **Investigated first, per the brief.** The avatar (`phPfAvatarHtml`, built 2026-10-09) already reads a photo by an `isProfile` flag on the existing per-patient photo store (`phRenPhotosFor`/IndexedDB), not a second copy — so "choose an existing photo" only ever needed a new WAY to set that flag, never a new place to store the picture. No existing "pick one photo from the gallery for an external purpose" picker exists anywhere in the app: the "info-letter picture picker" CLAUDE.md's own Photos section describes turned out to be `PH_TONGUE_SHOT_RANK`, an AUTOMATIC best-photo resolver (natural light > unlabelled > side > sublingual > flash) with no manual UI at all (`phLtrEnsureTonguePhoto`'s own comment: "the patient's LATEST tongue photo, automatic, no add-button"). So a new minimal sheet was built, cloned from the app's own shared `.ph-lk-sheet`/`.ph-lk-card` overlay shell (the same shell the "All formulas & criteria" and Linked symptoms sheets use), per the task's own fallback instruction.
- **Camera badge → menu → sheet, additive only.** `data-pf-avatar-add` still goes straight to the camera/file picker, pre-tagged `profile:true`, with NO extra tap, for a patient with nothing on file yet (`list.length > (pic ? 1 : 0)` false) — unchanged from her 2026-10-09 build, so the "nothing happens" regression she already complained about once can't recur. Once there's something to choose from, the same tap opens a tiny two-item menu (`phPfAvatarMenuFor`, one patient key at a time, view state only) instead: **Take a new photo** (identical `phRenCaptureStart(..., {profile:true})` call, unchanged) and **Choose from photos** (`phPfAvatarPickOpen`). Closes on an outside tap (inside `#pharmacyPage`, the house convention — a tap on `document.body` itself doesn't reach the delegated handler at all, by the app's own top-level guard, confirmed while testing) and on Esc.
- **The sheet** (`phPfAvatarPickOpen`/`phPfAvatarPickHtml`/`phPfAvatarPickBodyHtml`/`phPfAvatarPickTileHtml`): every photo already on file for that patient, newest first, each tile the thumbnail + its type/shot label + date (same label convention as the Records → Photos page: `"Tongue · <shot>"` or the plain type label); the current avatar's tile carries a ring + a check badge. Hooked into `phRenLoadPhotosFor`'s existing refresh chain (`if (phPfAvatarPickKey === patientKey) phPfAvatarPickRender();`, right beside `phPfAvatarRefresh`) so a photo added/renamed elsewhere while the sheet is open stays in sync, the same idiom every other photo-dependent surface in the file already uses. Empty state (a patient with photos loaded but zero on file — only reachable if she opens the sheet from somewhere that doesn't already gate it, since the badge menu itself never appears with nothing to choose from) reads "No photos on file yet." — two words + nothing else, not a suggestion.
- **The one write door, `phPfAvatarSetProfilePhoto(patientKey, photoId)`:** a fresh `phRenPhotoGetAllForPatient` read (never the render cache, which may carry a stale `objectUrl`-only shape), clears `isProfile` off whichever record currently holds it and sets it on the one she picked, each write going straight back through the existing `phRenPhotoPut` — the exact same precaution `phRenCaptureSave`'s own "profile" tag already takes (2026-10-09). **No image bytes are duplicated or re-stored** — the avatar continues reading the same blob the gallery already has, just pointed at a different existing record. Confirmation is `presSavedToast` ("Profile photo updated."), never `phFlashShow` (this sheet floats over a patient profile page; a flash there would rebuild the whole panel under it).
- **Pronoun-safe:** the sheet's subtitle reads through `phPro(name)` ("tap one to use it as **his/her/their** avatar"), not a hand-typed "her" — caught and fixed before testing, per the standing 2026-10-14 pronoun rule (the first draft had hand-typed "her" in two spots).
- **Phone-rule compliant:** no new standalone `@media (max-width: 640px)` block was added (an early draft added one to reposition the menu on a narrow column; removed once the menu was re-anchored `top: calc(100% + 4px); left: 0` instead of beside the badge, which needs no width-specific override at all — confirmed by measurement at 375px, no horizontal overflow).
- **Verified live** (this folder's dev-server slots were free this time — `preview_start` succeeded; the Browser pane's own sign-in overlay still blocks a real screenshot of a signed-in patient record, the same documented sandbox limitation hit repeatedly elsewhere in this file, so verification was computed-style/`getBoundingClientRect()`/state-assertion based, through REAL dispatched clicks and REAL IndexedDB reads/writes, not hand-poked function calls): a synthetic patient with 3 real IndexedDB photo records (one flagged `isProfile`) — clicking the badge opens the menu (2 buttons, correct labels); clicking "Choose from photos" opens the sheet with all 3 tiles sorted newest-first, the correct one ringed/ticked; clicking a DIFFERENT tile closes the sheet, shows the toast, and — confirmed via a completely fresh `phRenPhotoGetAllForPatient` re-read of the real IndexedDB store, not the in-memory cache — the `isProfile` flag genuinely moved to the new record and off the old one; the live avatar `<img>` was re-sampled pixel-by-pixel via canvas and matched the newly-picked photo's own colour exactly, confirming the avatar display reads back the real bytes, not a stale reference. A second synthetic patient with **zero** photos on file: clicking the badge skips the menu entirely and goes straight into `phRenCaptureStart` with the identical `{profile:true, type:"full"}` state the original 2026-10-09 build produced — the "take a new photo" path is provably unchanged. Outside-tap-closes and Esc-closes both confirmed (the first outside-tap attempt used `document.body.click()` directly and appeared to fail — traced to the app's own pre-existing `if (!e.target.closest("#pharmacyPage, #phShellFooter")) return;` top-level guard on that click handler, not a bug in this build; retested with a tap inside `#pharmacyPage`, which is what a real "tap elsewhere on the page" always is, and it closed correctly). 1280px and 375px: menu and sheet card both measured with zero horizontal overflow (`document.body.scrollWidth === window.innerWidth` exactly at 375px; the sheet's photo grid wraps to 2 columns at 375px with no overflow). No new console errors at any point (the one pre-existing error, "An unknown error occurred when fetching the script," is the known offline-sandbox external-script-fetch limitation documented elsewhere in this file, unrelated to this change). Test patient and all synthetic photo records were deleted from IndexedDB after verification.
- **Not exercised:** a real patient, her phone, a real screenshot of the signed-in app (the sandbox's sign-in overlay blocks it; every check above was done through real dispatched DOM events and real IndexedDB reads instead, which is a stronger guarantee of the actual write/read behaviour than a screenshot would have been, but a human eye hasn't looked at the pixels).
- **Disclosed judgement call:** when the patient has existing photos, the badge opens a menu rather than going straight to the picker sheet — a deliberate middle ground between "always show the menu" (an extra tap even for someone who always wants a fresh photo) and "always go straight to camera" (her literal original behaviour, which would have buried the new feature with no visible door). If she'd rather the badge open the picker sheet directly (with "+ Take a new photo" as a tile/chip inside it instead of a separate menu step), that's a quick follow-up, not a rebuild — the menu step is the only structural choice in this build that wasn't dictated by the existing code.

## Care Plan phase Formula: Fang Bing Ren's live top formula, fill-when-blank; phase-1-by-complaint confirmed already built (synth22 batch review, Workstream E, 2026-10-16; committed on `session-a` — LIVE on main (audited 2026-10-18: origin/main has since advanced past this build))
Her ask: "Link diagnosis and goal and phase with the chief complaint and secondary complaints... Fang bing ren is where i plan herbal formula, integrate that." A prior research pass found Diagnosis/Goal already auto-derive correctly (`phTpAutoDx`/`phTpAutoGoal`, untouched); the real gap was the Care Plan phase's Formula field never reading FBR's live ranking. She approved the proposed design verbatim: "Does the Care Plan↔MSK↔FBR design I proposed (phase shows FBR's live top formula as a fill-when-blank suggestion, same pattern as Points; plan picker already leads phase 1 by complaint) match what you want?" → "Yes, build it as proposed."

This build extends exactly that field — no new suggestion surface anywhere else. Clean fit, no conflict to flag.
- **Formula field** (`phTpLiveCtxRowHtml`, the Session grid's live-phase strip — the one read via `phTpLivePhase`, shown for the CURRENT phase only, on the Care Plan page's Course column): a new `phTpFbrLiveLead(rec, name)` (beside `phFbrLeadOf`) reads `phFbrRank`/`phFbrLeadOf` — the SAME ranking the Fang Bing Ren page itself shows — and returns `{id, name}` only when `hasTicks` is true (a real signal; never her declaration-order default lead with nothing behind it, which would read as a real formula when it is just the fallback).   - **Blank + no real FBR signal**: falls back to the template's own one-time `suggestFormula` default, reworded from the old "`<text>` *suggested*" to "`<text>` **(this plan's own default)**" — same mechanism (lower priority, untouched), wording fixed to a plain fact per the grep-for-suggest habit, since this exact line was being rewritten anyway. No formula at all → the existing quiet dash.
  - **Already hers (`ph.formulaName` typed/filled)**: shown plainly, exactly as before — **never** re-offered. If FBR's live lead has since moved to a DIFFERENT formula, one quiet line appears under it, "Fang Bing Ren's current lead: `<name>`" (informational only, not a tap target, not an action) — the same "hers vs auto, auto is informational once hers exists" pattern `phTpDxHersText`/`phTpGoalHersText` already use for Diagnosis/Goal. So "pain → phase 1 treats pain of that location first" is satisfied end to end by the EXISTING mechanism: her stated complaint leads the picker to the right template, and that template's own phase 1 is already the pain-first phase. No new phase-reordering logic was built — building one would have duplicated an already-correct mechanism, which is exactly the gap this task said to flag rather than guess at. No gap found to flag.
- **Verified** via a standalone headless-Edge harness (this folder's dev-server pool was held by concurrent sibling sessions, confirmed by the `preview_start` tool itself at the start of this task; fell back to the documented technique — the real `phTpLiveCtxRowHtml`/`phTpFbrLiveLead`/`phFbrRank`/`phFbrLeadOf` bodies run verbatim inside the FULL extracted app script, inlined into one HTML file so Chrome's cross-origin error-masking on a `file://` `<script src>` couldn't hide a real syntax error, then driven with synthetic `PHARMACY.patients` records and real plan/phase objects — never reimplemented stand-ins): the whole 103k-line script parses and boots with zero caught errors (confirming the edit introduced no syntax break anywhere in the file, not just locally); ## App-wide audit: "when I select chips, the screen flashes" — unconditional entrance animations replaying on every scoped repaint (her 2026-10-17 "do an audit for the whole app to fix this"; committed on `session-a` — LIVE on main (confirmed ancestor of origin/main as of the 2026-10-18 audit), build 20261017-1040000)
**Root cause, proved live, not guessed.** A chip tap on a scoped host (confirmed first on the Cycle page: tapping a calendar day) still does a wholesale `innerHTML` replace of a sizeable ancestor container (`.ph-assess-panel` and everything inside it) rather than patching only the thing that changed — the same "not a fine-grained DOM patch" shape CLAUDE.md already documents for several individual pages. That by itself only costs a reflow; the actual VISIBLE flash comes from a second, broader defect: several of the app's structural/card CSS classes carry an unconditional mount animation — `animation: phPfwRise .35s ease both` (and the matching `phPfRing`/`phRfcRise` families) — declared directly on the BASE class with no gating modifier (`.fresh`/`.in`/`.new`/`.pop`), so the instant the browser sees that class on a brand-new DOM node (which is every single repaint, since the whole container was just rebuilt), it replays the full rise/fade-in — for a `.ph-pf-onebox`-sized card, or a progress ring snapping back to 0% and re-filling, that reads as the screen "flashing" on an ordinary chip tap anywhere nearby. The existing codebase already half-recognised this: a `prefers-reduced-motion` override at (what was) line 8216 already disables `animation` on `.ph-pfw-start`/`.ph-pfw-card`/`.ph-pfw-branch`/`.ph-fbr-grp.enh` and a second one at ~15323-15328 does the same for `.ph-pf-statusline`/`.ph-pf-progress`/`.ph-pf-plantile`/`.ph-pf-cycring`/`.ph-pf-onebox` — proving these elements already work correctly with no animation at all; they just weren't turned off for everyone, only for accessibility.
- **Confirmed live, with instrumentation, before touching any code.** Built a synthetic patient through the real UI (`presStartNew`, the real "✓ Create patient" button, the real Start-here sex/DOB gate, the real no-plan gate's "Blank plan" card) rather than poking records directly, then: (1) a `MutationObserver` on the panel showed a single calendar-day tap replacing `.ph-assess-panel` (1 node added/removed at that level) plus `.ph-uc-body w` (the Usual period wheel) and `.ph-band-sub`, confirming the repaint's blast radius reaches well past the clicked element; (2) `document.getAnimations()` immediately after that same tap listed 12 running animations, including one squarely on `.ph-pfw-card.uc` (the Usual period card) — the exact card sitting on that page, replaying its mount animation from an unrelated calendar tap.
- **Fixed by removing the animation declaration from the base (ungated) selector only** — every rule below keeps its border/background/padding/etc. exactly as it was, only the `animation:` (and its matching `animation-delay:` where present) came out: `.ph-cc`, `.ph-cc-fold`, `.ph-pf-spark`, `.ph-pat-shape`, `.ph-fbr-grp.enh`, `.ph-pfw-start`, `.ph-pfw-branch`, `.ph-pfw-card`, `.ph-pf-progress`, `.ph-pf-ring`, `.ph-pf-plantile`, `.ph-pf-cycring`, `.ph-pf-onebox`, `.ph-cc2` (Patient details' Came in for / one-box cluster — likely her single most-tapped surface), plus the Formula refill workbench's own matching pattern (`.ph-rfc-picked`, `.ph-rfc-shortbar`, `.ph-rfc .chips`). **Deliberately left untouched:** every animation already gated behind a transient, JS-managed modifier class (`.in`, `.pop`, `.fresh`, `.new`, `.draw`, `.drop`, `.glow`, `.sweep`, `.anim`, `.enter`, `.rise`, `.go`) — those are a different, lower-risk category (a one-shot class a handler adds/removes, not baked into every render) and were not audited line-by-line in this pass; a few of the ~85 `animation: … both` rules in the file still fall in that bucket and were read but not touched.
- **Verified live, before and after, on two independent surfaces, with the real edited file (not a patched stylesheet) after a full navigate/reload:** (1) Cycle page — the identical calendar-day tap that showed 12 running animations (including `.ph-pfw-card.uc`) before the fix now shows **zero** running animations after it. (2) Patient details — typing a chief complaint into the Came in for box and committing it (real `input`/`change`/Enter events on the real `[data-cc-add-in]` field) now shows only 3 running animations, all correctly transient and intentional (`.ph-pf-avatar-add.nudge`, `.ph-cc2-sv.show` the "Saved ✓" fade, and a session-pip growth bar) — none of them `.ph-cc2`/`.ph-pf-onebox`/`.ph-pf-progress`/`.ph-pf-ring` restarting. `getComputedStyle(...).animationName` on both `.ph-cc2` and `.ph-pf-onebox` reads `"none"`; the earlier 2026-10-15 z-index fix on `.ph-cc2` (`position: relative; z-index: 2`) is confirmed still intact. No new console errors at any point; synthetic test patient and script deleted from the sandbox after verification.
- **Scope, disclosed honestly rather than overclaimed:** this fixes every surface built on `phPfwRise`/`phPfRing`/`phRfcRise` applied to a base (ungated) class — which covers the Came in for card (both pages), the Patient-details one-box cluster, the progress ring and plan tile, the Cycle ring, every `.ph-pfw-*` question-set card (Usual period, change-of-life, men's, Pain intake — anything built on the shared question-card shell), the Fang Bing Ren grouped sign board, and the Formula refill workbench's fix-short/chip rows. It does **not** cover every possible flash in the app: the ~85 total `animation: … both` declarations include several dozen already gated behind a transient class, which were read but not individually tested for the same "baked into every render, not JS-added on genuine mount" failure mode — if she still sees a flash on a SPECIFIC page after this lands, that page's own animation is the next one to check, not a sign this fix didn't work. The underlying "scoped repaint still does a wholesale innerHTML swap of a container bigger than what changed" pattern (the MutationObserver finding) was also not rearchitected — removing the animation fixes the visible symptom without needing to rebuild every repaint function into a fine-grained DOM patch, which would be a much larger, separate undertaking.
- **Not exercised:** a real patient, her phone, a real screenshot (the sandbox's sign-in-overlay/hidden-pane limitation this file already documents repeatedly — verification here used `document.getAnimations()`, `MutationObserver` and `getComputedStyle` instead, which is a more precise instrument for an animation-timing bug than a screenshot would have been, but no human eye has looked at the pixels). A sweep of the remaining `.in`/`.pop`/`.fresh`-gated animations for the same "is this class baked into the render output or added by JS on genuine mount" question was not done — flagged as a reasonable next step if she reports the flash persisting on a specific screen.

## Pain → cause link: a clinical finding can be marked the cause of a pain (her 2026-10-17: "there are things that patient complain about, and there are clinical findings that tell me is the cause of complaint ... its not a secondary complaint", mock `pain-cause-link-mock-2026-10-17.html`, her verbatim approval "Yes, build it"; committed on `session-a` — LIVE on main (audited 2026-10-18: origin/main has since advanced past this build))
Her example: ankle pain, then on exam the calf and hamstring are found tight — the tightness is the CAUSE of the pain, not a second, unrelated complaint. Full process: 8 clarifying questions over two rounds (all her picks), a detailed visual mock, her explicit "Yes, build it" (MOCK = BUILD exactly).
- **`causes[]` on a pain entry** (`plan.painMap[]` / `rec.painSites[]`): `[{type:"muscle"|"rom"|"mmt"|"test"|"fbr"|"note", key, kind?, text?}]` — a REFERENCE to today's own exam data or a Fang Bing Ren sign, or a free-typed note, never a copy; the display label always resolves live (`phPmCauseLabel`) so it stays current even as today's exam changes, falling back to a plain name if that finding no longer shows today. `causes` added to `phPmWrite`'s write-whitelist (alongside the pre-existing `dx`/`main` protections — a documented past trap on this function: a field left off that whitelist is silently dropped on the very next write).
- **The picker** (`phPmCausePickerHtml`, opened by a "+ Likely cause" button under each pain row): three groups of real, derived facts she taps to link — today's palpation findings (`phPmCauseMuscleOpts`: tender/taut/trigger-band muscles), today's objective exam (`phPmCauseExamOpts`: weak strength, a positive special test, a painful or limited ROM movement), and her currently-true Fang Bing Ren signs (`phPmCauseFbrOpts`, Bing + Ren, sex-filtered) — plus a free-text "Or write it" note. Real derived facts she explicitly taps, never an app-generated suggestion (her no-suggestions standing rule).
- **Both directions, one link.** The pain table's "Caused by" row (`phPmTableHtml`, Musculoskeletal page only — `sc`, the only place today's exam data exists to pick from) shows the linked causes as chips with a ×; the Palpation tab's muscle table (`phMskPalpHtml`) gained a reciprocal "Cause of" column: a muscle with no link shows a "→ mark as cause of…" BUTTON (not plain coloured text — see the TAPPABLE THINGS fix below) opening the same picker from the finding side, listing today's pains; a muscle already linked shows a quiet "→ contributes to: <pain>" tag (`phPmCauseContribs`, a live reverse-scan of the pains' own `causes[]`, never a second stored copy).
- **TAPPABLE THINGS self-correction, mid-build:** the mock drew "→ mark as cause of…" as plain coloured text (an ACT control — it opens a picker). Caught before shipping: her LOCKED standing rule bans plain-coloured-text taps even when a mock drew it that way (a mock is approved for its CONTENT, not a license to violate a separate locked rule it happens to depict literally). Restyled `.arrow-act` to a proper 6px-corner, 1.5px-`--ph-herb`-outlined button (28px tall), keeping the "→" as decorative text inside the correctly-shaped control — consistent with the "data arrows" exception already carved out for `.contrib` (a fact display, not an action).
- **Write doors:** `phPmCauseToggle` (pick-from-picker, true toggle), `phPmCauseAddNote`, `phPmCauseRemoveAt` — all through `phPmWrite`. Every write refreshes both surfaces together (`phMskRefresh(["exam","nprs"])`, the established scoped-repaint mechanism, confirmed to also trigger `phPmTblRefresh()`), so the pain-table chip and the Palpation reciprocal tag can never disagree.
- Verified end-to-end through the real functions on a synthetic patient (never a hand-typed stand-in): a Gastrocnemius "taut band" palpation finding surfaces correctly in the muscle picker group, links to an ankle pain, resolves its live label ("Gastrocnemius (Right) · taut band") on both the pain-table chip and the reciprocal "→ contributes to" tag; a Fang Bing Ren sign (`cold_extrem`, "Hands & feet: cold") surfaces correctly in that picker group and links the same way; a free-typed note links and displays; removing the muscle cause correctly reverts the reciprocal side back to showing the "→ mark as cause of…" button once contribs become empty (confirmed `hasMarkAsCauseBtn:true` after removal); all three cause types coexist on one pain and resolve independently. Rendered the pain table at phone width (375px) inside the real `#pharmacyPage` stylesheet and confirmed the restyled `.arrow-act` computes as a real button (1.5px `--ph-herb` border, 6px radius, 28px height) — not plain text.
- **Not exercised:** a real patient, her phone, a real click dispatched through the document-level delegated handlers (`data-pm-cause-toggle`/`-pick`/`-rm`, `data-msk="cause-open"`/`"cause-pick"`) — this sandbox's `phPatientProfileOpen` call rendered an empty `#presPanel` with no console error (a known gap in this session's harness, not traced further), so every write/read above was exercised through the documented "synthetic patient through real functions" technique rather than a live tap; a second, not-yet-linked muscle finding tested side by side with an already-linked one on the Palpation tab.

## Came in for timeline: labels overlapping on a dense cluster of complaints (her 2026-10-17 screenshot of Jason Walsh + "see the problem?", build 20261017-1090000)
Her screenshot: several complaints dated within a few days of each other (clots, light shoulders, slight neck pain, the main complaint, painful periods, period cramps) printed their labels on top of each other.
- **Root cause:** `phCcRoadHtml`'s label-packing only ever had 4 fixed tiers (`up`, `dn`, `up2`, `dn2`). Once a 5th complaint landed close to the others, its fallback branch picked whichever of the 4 tiers had the MOST clearance even when that clearance was nowhere near the 22% minimum — silently printing its label over an earlier one instead of ever failing loudly.
- **Fix:** the two-named-tier system is now an unbounded alternating up/dn stack — each side is a growing array of "the left% last placed at this tier," so a dense cluster just grows the row taller instead of ever reusing an occupied slot. `.t-up2`/`.t-dn2` CSS classes are gone; every dot now carries its own `--to` (pixel offset) custom property instead, so the CSS needs only `.t-up`/`.t-dn`. `ax`/`h` (axis position / row height) are computed from however many tiers each side actually used, not a fixed on/off switch for a 2nd tier.
- Verified live (real `phCcRoadHtml` calls, not reimplemented): her exact scenario (8 points, several sharing one date) now renders with zero overlapping label rectangles; a stress case of 11 points all on the SAME date also renders with zero overlaps (the row grows to 546px tall instead of stacking); the ordinary 2-point case still renders byte-identical to before (`--h:150px;--ax:70px`, no behaviour change for the common case).
- **Not exercised:** a real patient, her phone, a real screenshot.

Follows directly from the Pain table's "one combobox" build above. Two asks in one session: apply the same datalist-combobox pattern to every other "how long" mechanism in the app, then extend the shared parser to also accept a bare year or "mm/yyyy" when she doesn't know the exact day.

- **Shared parser, one pair of functions, used everywhere:** `phCcParseDatePrec(t)` returns `{iso, prec, est}` or `null` — a duration ("2 yr") still resolves via the existing `phCcParseDate` with `prec:"d", est:true`; a bare 4-digit year (1900–this year) gives `prec:"y", est:false`; "mm/yyyy" gives `prec:"m", est:false`; anything else falls through to `phCcParseDate` for a full date, `prec:"d", est:false`. `phCcFmtDatePrec(s, prec)` is its display twin (year alone / "mm/yyyy" / full "dd/mm/yyyy"). Both sit right after the existing `phCcParseDate`/`phCcFmtDate` pair and are reused by the Pain table, Came-in-for's day box, and nowhere else yet (the Treatment table's since-editor was a disclosed, deliberate scope cut — see below).
- **Pain table**: a new `sincePrec` field on each pain entry (`p.sincePrec`, `"m"`/`"y"`, absent = day), added to `phPmWrite`'s write-whitelist (the documented past trap — a field left off that list is silently dropped on the next write) alongside the pre-existing `dx`/`main`/`causes` protections. The since box's `change` handler now reads through `phCcParseDatePrec` and stores both `since` (always the ISO date) and `sincePrec`; the box's displayed value uses `phCcFmtDatePrec(p.since, p.sincePrec)` so a year-only or month-only entry is never expanded into a fake full date. Deliberately did NOT re-normalize the box's text immediately after a typed duration or datalist pick (e.g. typing "2 yr" still shows "2 yr" until the next full repaint) — matches the pre-existing behaviour, a self-caught scope-discipline correction rather than a new feature.
- **Came in for card**: the day box's own separate `<select>` + "Custom" chip (built earlier the same day, alongside the Day/Month/Year precision bar) is gone — the day box itself now carries `list="phCcSinceList"`, the identical mechanism. Its `change` handler reads through `phCcParseDatePrec` too, so typing "2026" or "08/2026" directly into the day box works without switching to the Month/Year tab first; `phCcMainSinceSet`/`phCcSecSinceSet` (which already take a `prec` argument from the earlier precision-bar build) needed no changes — confirmed by reading them, not assumed.
- **Treatment table (`phTsSinceEditHtml`)**: the old 7-chip quick-pick row is gone; the dd/mm/yyyy box now carries `list="phTsSinceList"` with a `<datalist>` of `["Today", ...5 of PH_CC_QUICK, "First assessment"]` (same options the chips used to offer). The now-dead `act === "since-q"` branch in the click dispatcher was removed. The `data-ts-since-in` `change` handler now special-cases the literal strings "today" and "first assessment" (case-insensitive) before falling through to `phCcParseDatePrec`, taking only `.iso` and discarding `.prec`/`.est` — **a disclosed, deliberate scope cut**: this field has no existing precision-storage equivalent to `sincePrec` (its `rec.tri`-backed store only ever held a resolved date), and adding one was judged a separate design decision (parallel precision store vs. silently dropping it) rather than something to improvise mid-build; she can ask for it explicitly if the month/year typing matters here too.
- Verified live via a real dev-server preview + direct calls to the real, unmodified functions (not reimplemented stand-ins): `phCcParseDatePrec`/`phCcFmtDatePrec` resolve all four shapes correctly (year, mm/yyyy, duration, full date) and correctly reject an out-of-range year/month; `phTsSinceEditHtml` renders with `list="phTsSinceList"` and all 7 datalist options including "Today" and "First assessment"; `phCcTableHtml`'s rendered output carries the `phCcSinceList` datalist with all 11 `PH_SINCE_OPTS`; the app booted with zero new console errors after every edit (the dead `since-q` removal, the Treatment-table change-handler rewrite). Confirmed via grep that no reference to the old `data-pm-qsel`/`data-cc-main-qsel`/`data-cc-sec-qsel`/`act === "since-q"` branches remains anywhere in the file.
- **Not exercised:** a real patient, her phone, a real tap through any of the three native browser datalist pickers themselves, a real screenshot, the Treatment table's "Today"/"First assessment" special-casing through an actual dispatched `change` event (verified by reading the handler and by the shared-parser unit checks above, not by a live click).

## Saved-toast ("Filed as …") text unreadable: a missing colour fallback, not a style guess (her 2026-10-19 screenshot of a Records → Photos label-toast, "tis is hard to read", build 20261019-1260000)
Her screenshot: a dark teal pill reading "Filed as Skin  Undo" — "Undo" crisp white, the message text dim/near-illegible against the dark background.
- **Root cause, traced, not guessed:** `presSavedToast` (`.ph-saved-toast`, THE one body-level toast since the 2026-10-15 "One toast" audit) is appended with `document.body.appendChild(el)` — genuinely OUTSIDE `#pharmacyPage`'s DOM subtree. Its CSS sets `color: var(--ph-cream)` with **no fallback value**, but `--ph-cream` is only ever defined inside the `#pharmacyPage { ... }` rule block (line ~358), never on bare `:root`. A CSS custom property is scoped to the DOM subtree of the selector that defines it — at a body-level element outside `#pharmacyPage`, `var(--ph-cream)` is invalid at computed-value time, so `color` (an inherited property) silently falls through to whatever `<body>`'s own ambient text colour is, rather than the intended near-white `#EEF5F7`. The pill's `background: var(--ph-green-deep, #0B3B4B)` on the very same line already carries a fallback, so the dark background always rendered correctly — only the text colour was silently broken, exactly matching "Undo" staying crisp (its colour is hardcoded `#fff`) while the message dimmed.
- **Fix, one token:** `color: var(--ph-cream)` → `color: var(--ph-cream, #EEF5F7)` — the same fallback pattern the background declaration on the same line already uses.
- **Verified before shipping:** built a standalone reproduction (the real CSS declaration, both the buggy and fixed versions, with `--ph-cream` scoped to a sibling `#pharmacyPage` block the toast sits outside of, matching the real DOM relationship exactly) and screenshotted via headless Edge — the "before" render reproduced her exact symptom (dim, low-contrast message text, crisp white Undo); the "after" render showed both at full, matching contrast.
- **Concurrent-session care, disclosed:** a second session had uncommitted Care Plan page work ("simplify the full Care Plan page") sitting in the same `index.html` at the time. Extracted only this fix's own 2 hunks (the colour fallback + the routine meta-build-tag bump) via a `-U3` context patch applied with `git apply --cached`, verified via `git diff --cached` vs. the remaining `git diff`, and committed with no paths — their work was left untouched in the working tree, not swept in.
- **Not exercised:** a real patient, her phone, a post-push screenshot of the signed-in app. This fix applies to every `presSavedToast`/`phCycToast` call app-wide (saves, copies, Undo bars, the Records → Photos labelling flow) — all share the one `.ph-saved-toast` rule, so none of them needed a separate fix.

## Findings trend: Grid/Trail table of dated Tongue and Abdomen findings (her ask, full mock/review cycle, final "Yes, build it"; mock `findings-trend-table-mock.html`; build 20261019-1260100)
A way to visually track Tongue and Abdomen clinical findings across visit dates in table format, so changes/trends are visible at a glance. Her confirmed picks from the review (not re-asked): Grid default (date columns, newest left, mirroring her own Photos Comparison table precedent), a Grid|Trail toggle, a door on EACH exam page into ONE shared sheet, everything on file (no date cutoff), a changed cell opens that dated visit, a diagram row above the word rows drawn by the real renderers — never a second, hand-drawn tongue/abdomen shape.
- **One new sheet, `phFtOpen`/`phFtCardHtml`/`phFtRender`/`phFtClose`** (module-level `phFtPatient`/`phFtExam`/`phFtView`, reset on close, nothing written to `rec`), cloned 1:1 from the app's own shared `.ph-lk-sheet`/`.ph-lk-card` overlay shell and open/close/Esc/backdrop-tap pattern (copied from `phFbrAllRefOpen`/`phFbrAllRefClose`/`phFbrAllRefRender`, the "All formulas & criteria" sheet). The Abdomen|Tongue tab and the Grid|Trail switch both reuse the exam pages' own `.ph-tng2-seg`/`.ph-ltr-qual` segmented-chip-bar (her confirmed 2026-10-16 standard for one-category chip groups) — no new switch component.
- **Data, read-only, reused not reinvented:** `phFtDates(rec, kind)` walks `rec.acuSessions`, reads each dated `rec.visitFnd[s.id]` through the real `phVisitFndRead` (the same accessor the exam pages, Visit checks (`presVisitChecksHtml`) and the Care Plan's session folds already use), and adds today's standing `rec.tongueExam`/`rec.abdomen.chart` when nothing has been logged to a session yet today — newest first, everything on file, no cutoff. `phFtTngVals`/`phFtAbdVals` group the real field names `phTng2Read`/`phAbd2Read` already define (Tongue: `colour`/`colourMore`/`colourAt`, `shape`+`thickness`+`deviation`, `moist`, `coatThick`/`coatColour`/`coatQual`, `under`, `marks`; Abdomen: `tension`/`tensionAt`, and `marks.cold`/`warm`/`water`/`gas`/`tender`/`xiaxin`/`pulsation`/`bulging`/`sunken`/`tightrect`/`distended`/`thinwall`) into the six Tongue rows and four Abdomen rows her mock named — nothing invented, nothing hand-typed.
- **The real renderers, not a second drawing:** the Diagram row (Grid's top row, Trail's first track) calls `phTongueChartSvg(r.tng, null, {ro:true})` / `phAbdChartSvg(r.abd, null, {ro:true, legacy:r.zones})` directly, wrapped in the exact `.ph-visit-tng.ro.mini`/`.ph-visit-abd-map.ro.mini` classes the Visit checks table's own mini-charts already use (`presVisitChecksHtml`) — the same CSS sizing, no new size rule invented.
- **"Changed" cells:** `phFtEq` compares a row's value array (order-independent) against the visit immediately before it (Grid: `dates[i+1]`; Trail, reversed to oldest-first: `dates[i-1]`); only flags a change when BOTH the cell and its predecessor are non-empty (an empty-to-filled or filled-to-empty transition is never "changed," matching the mock). The ring reuses the existing, non-reserved `--ph-purple`/`-deep`/`-tint` token family (already used elsewhere for a different "T-test" category marker) rather than inventing a new accent — gold stays reserved for status per the house rule.
- **Tap-to-open, reusing the app's own navigation, not a new one:** a populated cell with a real logged session (`hasSession:true`) renders as a `<button data-flow-prof="checks">` — the exact existing attribute/handler that already routes to the Visit checks tab (`presAssessTab = "checks"`); today's own standing draft (no session logged yet) renders as a plain, non-interactive cell instead, since there is nothing dated to "jump to" — she is already looking at it on the exam page the door was opened from.
- **Doors:** `phExamPageHtml` (the shared wrapper for the Tongue/Pulse/Abdomen exam pages) grows one conditional row, `id === "tongue" || id === "abdomen"` only (never Pulse) — an outlined `.ph-rtng-act` button (the existing 6px-corner "act" button shape, already used for "Change type"/"Change date" on the Ren photo viewer) with the sprite's existing `#i-chart` icon, defaulting the sheet's tab to whichever page it opened from.
- **Disclosed judgment calls, her instructions didn't cover these:** (1) the mock's "+ Add today's" button on an empty today-cell was deliberately **not** carried into the real build — the patient workflow LAW states the exam pages are the ONLY entry for a dated finding (Phase 2), so a second inline "add" affordance on a read-only trend sheet would contradict it; every empty cell (today's or a past visit's) just reads "none yet," plain text, no action.
