## Me on the grid: a stack instead of slivers (2026-10-25; commit 5ffbcb1d, LIVE in build 20261025-100100, carried by another session's publish; her "push live")
- **Her ask:** a screenshot of her live week at 1219px with Me on All: beside patient bookings her routines were cut into unreadable slivers ("|", "!", "T"), at 3pm (Code + Lunch beside three patients), 6pm Mon / Tue (Travel + Shoulder Rehab), and Saturday. The routine times were right; the layout split the 26% side lane between every item that met a booking (`26 / of`).
- **The fix:** an item is never narrower than the lane. A cluster whose columns would split it (2+ beside a booking, 4+ on a day with no booking) folds into ONE stack over its whole span (`phC22DayLayout` builds `{stk:[...], s, e, side}`; `phC22LifeHtml` hands it to `phC22StkHtml`): the count, then each item's glyph in its own colour (a dot when it has none, `phC22Mark`). A tap opens its card (`stk:<day>|<id>|…`, `phC22StkPopHtml`): the day, the span, a 32px row per item (faint tint of its colour, title, start). A row opens that item's own card (Done · Edit), still hanging off the stack (`phApptPopAnchorEl` finds the stack by `data-ph-c22-ids~=`, never a row inside the card). Tapping the stack again closes it; Enter / Space open it; every "clear the ring" list now includes the stack.
- **Calls made (disclosed):** the thresholds (2 beside a booking, 4 on an open day, so nothing drops under the lane's own width); a single item in the lane is unchanged; the stack's edge is the neutral grey (its items have different colours); the card is the same small 240px card as an item's.
- **Tested (localhost:8947, a test owner tag + her routine shape as test data, no sign-in):** 1280, 7 days: 6 stacks (Mon 3pm Code + Lunch, Mon 6pm Travel + Shoulder Rehab, Tue 3pm Code + Lunch + Dentist, Wed / Thu / Sat 3pm), each 28px wide with the count and marks; no lane item under 28px. Card: 3 rows, 32px, own tints, on screen beside the stack; a row → "Dentist / Tue 27 Oct · 3:30 – 4:30 / Done / Edit", the stack keeps its ring; Done → ✓ Done; close → focus back on the stack, no ring left; Enter opens a stack; a second tap closes it; Code's row → Edit → the dialog on Me, This day | Every day. Events level: 0 stacks, ⟳ counts; ⟳ on Monday → its two stacks. 375 (1 day): stacks 77px, the card a bottom sheet with 343px rows, no sideways scroll. Prescriptions search: "alice" → 1 of 2, cleared → 2. No console errors (two 404s from the harness).

## Appointments grid: seamless (2026-10-25)
Her ask (Google Calendar beside the LCM week): "i ike the spacing from google calendar, seamless. make mock of calendar in lcm." Mock `calendar-seamless-mock-2026-10-25.html` (artifact 9kqqqmTGMrNUHUo94fwMnJ); her 8 picks, all the recommended ones; "build it".
- **Look (CSS, Appointments calendar block ~4097-4210):** blocks edge to edge, 6px corners, no shadow, a 1px white seam (`box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #fff`); hour hairlines only (`#E6EDF0`, the half-hour gradient and the long-day `i.hh` rules are gone), no today wash; hover = `filter: brightness(1.05)`, no scale; blocks stack by `--z` (3 + column), hover 20, open card 19, search match 18.
- **Day head:** small MON over a big date (display font, 24px; 17px in a 28px circle at ≤900px), today's date in a teal circle, the visit count and the month are gone. The `${cake}` slot stays where it was (the one-calendar session renames it).
- **Nesting (`phApptCalDayBlocks` + `phApptCalBlockStyle`):** a cluster whose visits all start together (`it.same`) shares the width in halves; otherwise column 0 is full width and a later column sits over it from 45% across (each further one 15% more, 75% at most), `--z` keeps later ones on top.
- **Behind (`phApptCalGridHtml`):** a visit that meets one of her own grid events gets `it.under` and is drawn 10px in, so the event's colour shows at its left. `b.narrow` from `phC22DayLayout` is no longer read. Her events' own lane / dashed look is the one-calendar session's (`phC22LifeHtml`, `.ph-c22-*`), asked to go full width, solid tint, behind.
- **Fills the window:** `phApptCalEndFor` = the last booking's end rounded up to the half hour (4 hours at least; nothing booked keeps 7 AM - 9 PM); `phApptCalPxm` = the measured room / the span (34px an hour at least, 180 at most); the long-day map's busy stretches share the room the free bands leave. `phPinApptZones` reads the room off the body's own min-height (100dvh less the chrome: `innerHeight` disagreed with `dvh` by 20px in the pane) and redraws once (60ms debounce, latest room wins, at most 3 in 1.5s, never with a card open or while typing in the search; the first open keeps its rise-in). First open guesses `innerHeight - 190`. A phone keeps 66px an hour. The now line hides past the end (`phApptCalNowTick`).
- **Tested (Browser pane, localhost:8994, seeded bookings + her events through a stubbed `phC22Src`):** 1280x800 week: the grid ends at the last booking, body 614px = room 614px, no inner scroll; 9:30 / 10:30 / 11:00 nest (11:00 at 45%), two 2:00s in halves, a visit over Travel 10px in; teal circle on today. 375x760: 66px an hour, no sideways scroll, circles 28px. Prescriptions search narrows live and returns. No console errors from the grid.
- **Pages checked:** Appointments (week grid desktop + phone, day head), Prescriptions (search).
- **Not tested:** her real week with Cliniko colours; the Key2's 360 x 469; her own events drawn behind (waits on the one-calendar session's `phC22LifeHtml` change).
- **LIVE:** build 20261025-100100 (her "push live"; the stack fold 5ffbcb1d and the Me Routines list 71234172 rode along).

Her synth22 after the Me build went live: "as the only person that uses lcm, i want to be able to balance my life commitments and work commitment. i want the calendar to be a one space where i can see and manage work and life. need peoples birthdays to be visible. need to be able to take care of myself e.g. lunch breakfast fitness etc. i need a sleek design that holds alot of functions but is simple in design", with screenshots: "i need to see my whole page" (the grid cut at 3 PM; Lunch / Code slivers beside a patient; Breakfast / Gym chips on every day), "see birthdays and all day events", "i want to click and drag events", "i want my cycle day to show like birthdays". Guide `one-calendar-guide-2026-10-25.html`, mock `one-calendar-mock-2026-10-25.html` (MOCK = BUILD); her 13 picks; "build it". Built on the seamless grid (the other session's build the same day, which took pick 5: the hours fill the window).
- **Her picks:** 1 birthdays = cake + name + age chip in the row above the day · 2 cycle day in the DATE LINE ("CD 25"; a period day rose with the drop; the expected period a dashed rose pill) · 3 read from her OWN patient record's Cycle page, the record picked ONCE in the Me drawer · 4 routines = ONE ⟳ chip whose ring fills as they are ticked, tap unfolds · 5 clinic hours fill the window · 6 a routine that meets a patient = a faint full-width BAND behind the patients with its name in a pill at the right edge, never a lane; a one-off stays a block · 7 evenings = one ⟳ under the day · 8 her things drag: move (15-minute snap, a time tag) and stretch (bottom edge), a repeating one This day | Every day, toast + Undo · 9 a dragged PATIENT block drops into Edit prefilled, Save confirms · 10 cross-day drops in the week view · 11 tick = one tap on the pill, the second undoes, ✎ opens the card · 12 phone: same row, CD and drag (long-press lifts) · 13 "yes, mock it".

## 2026-10-26 · Lighter update check (what made LCM heavy)
- **Her ask:** "look at what makes LCM heavy" (the folder audit had noted the Key2 page weight).
- **Measured** (live build 20261025-211400): the page the phone gets is 7.77 MB, 1.76–1.81 MB compressed: code 1.46 MB (83%), styles 0.27 MB, icons almost nothing. What each area adds compressed: pictures 181 KB, Fang Bing Ren / Ren / Patterns / Guide 173, Care Plan & Treatment 150, tap and key handlers 140 (most of it the one 507 KB binding block in `renderPharmacy`), patient pages 86, Today's visit 83, Appointments 75, Cycle / IVF 73, Messages 66, Stock 64, Pain 52, Me 47, the exams 43, everything else 208. Removing spacing would save 3% only. No single area dominates.
- **The bigger cost was how often it travels and what it left behind:**
  1. `phUpdateCheck` fetched the whole page at `?probe=<time>` with `cache:"no-store"` 20 s after opening, every 5 minutes, and each time the tab came back: 1.8 MB each time (about 22 MB an hour while open).
  2. sw.js's cache-first branch stored every probe: one 7–10 MB copy per check, kept until the gold Update activates a new worker (sandbox: 16, then 23 copies, 163 MB; +21 MB in seconds). The 2026-10-14 photo eviction came from disk pressure on a nearly full disk, so this likely contributed (not proven on her machine).
  3. sw.js fetched every navigation with `no-store`, so every open downloaded the full page even when nothing had changed.
- **Fixed:**
  - `phUpdateCheck`: one fixed address `PH_PROBE_URL` (`?probe=1`) with `cache:"no-cache"` (GitHub Pages answers an unchanged page with a 304 and no body); reads only the page's head (`phProbeHead`, stops at the stamp or 64 KB); sweeps stored probe copies out of LCM's own `lcm-` caches before and after (`phProbeSweep`), so an older worker still active on a device can neither answer from its cache nor pile copies up. The compare and the button logic are unchanged.
  - sw.js: `probe=` requests pass straight through (never cached); navigations use `no-cache` (it still asks the server every time, so the 2026-08-19 reason for the cache mode still holds); each page's offline copy sits under its own key (the app as "./", chart.html and intake.html under their own path; opening chart.html used to overwrite the app's offline copy).
- **When it takes effect:** the page part on her first open of the next build (the first check per open downloads once, then 304s); the sw.js part when she presses the gold Update (the new worker also deletes the old cache with every stored copy in it).
- **Tested** (sandbox port 8994, and live GitHub Pages): with the old worker active, 23 stored copies became 1 after a check and stayed 1 after a second; the check read 458 KB of the 10 MB page and stopped; a temporary page stamped 20991231-000000 revealed the gold Update button through the real `phUpdateCheck` text, and the same build did not; with the new worker activated, the app booted, "./" held the app, a check stored nothing, chart.html was kept under its own key with "./" still the app, and with the server stopped the app opened from its offline copy; Prescriptions search narrowed (Tess shown, Zara and Mona hidden) and returned; from a browser on GitHub Pages, the first ask was 1,809,175 bytes and the second 300 bytes. The temporary page was binned after.
- **Not tested:** her real devices (the Key2 on 4G, the clinic computer); a real new build arriving through the full Update flow; how many stored copies her devices hold now (that needs her Chrome).
- **Pages checked:** Appointments (boot), Prescriptions list and search, My Cycle (chart.html). Nothing on screen looks different.

Mock `herb-schedule-mock-2026-10-26.html` (Artifact "Herbal Schedule"), 12 popup picks, then "Yes": all three are hard (remembering, which and when, running out) · **set clock times, she types them, nothing pre-filled** ("i decide") · tick in all three places (calendar, Me drawer, Herbs page) · on the calendar **its own block** · due = **glows gold** until ticked · running low = **N days left + Dispense** · two formulas = **a row each** · a fasting day keeps the doses at her times · a late tick counts any time that day · a new prescription **takes over by itself, keeping her times**.
- **Which prescription** (`phHbRows`, derived on read, nothing copied): scripts on her own record (the My profile name). The scripts dispensed on her **latest dispense day** are the schedule, one row each (that is how "takes over" and "a row each" fit together: a dispense on a later day replaces the earlier set; two scripts dispensed the same day are two rows); nothing dispensed yet = her record's own script, from today. Dose text / instruction: `schedPrepDosageText` / `schedPrepInstructionText` (the stored-script reads); dose days: `phFuDayPredicate` (Days it cannot read = every day); runs out: that dispense's follow-up (`PHARMACY.followups`, the Follow-ups page's own date), else `phFollowupCalc`. Days left = dose days from today to that day; "Last day"; "Ran out <day>" (red); a fortnight after it ran out the row leaves.
- **Data (her Me row, both logins):** `d.hbt` = {sid: {id, at: ["HH:MM" | ""], up}} her times (a script with none of its own reads her latest set: a new prescription keeps her times); `d.hbk` = {"day|sid|i": {id, at ISO, up, del?}} a dose taken. Merged entry by entry (`phHbNorm` / `phHbMerge` / `phHbAhead` beside the fasts in `phMeNormData` / `phMeMerge` / `phMeAhead`).
- **Where:** a **Herbs** step in the Mine group after Fasting (`RANK` 7.65; count "1/2" beside it, `phHbRailMini`) = `phHbPageHtml`: a card per prescription (jar, name, dose · instruction, days left + **Dispense** = her prescription open on Dispense), Times (time fields; on a phone without the clock icon so both sit on one line), Today (a chip per dose, tap = taken), Week (the last 7 days, today last, as the mock: a row per dose, filled = taken, dashed = not taken, a dash = no dose, "n of m"). **Me drawer:** a Herbs section under Today's meals, a tick per dose today, days left on the first row (`phHbDrwHtml`). **Grid:** each dose its own 15-minute block in her herb green `#15803D` with a leaf (`phHbDayItems` joins `phC22Src`; `phC22Ic` leaf; `phHbAct` / `phHbCls` in `phC22LifeHtml` and `phC22FoldHtml`): today's tap toggles taken with Undo, another day's opens its card (`phHbPopHtml`, also a stack's row); an untimed dose folds into the row above the day; on a phone outside the patients' hours they are the chips above / below. **⋯ menu:** Herbs beside Fasting. Every surface carries the same key (`data-ph-hb-tk`); a write repaints them all (`phHbRepaint`: `phMeRepaint(true)`, the page, the rail) and pops the ticked one; a dose turns gold in place the minute its time comes (30 s timer, no repaint). A time typed while its field has focus is saved quietly and the page repaints when she leaves the field (Enter saves at once): no repaint under her typing, no jump from one time box to the next.
- **Colours:** taken = `--ph-good`; due = a gold ring (`--ph-gold`, her pick); days left = `--ph-low` amber, ran out = `--ph-zero`; blocks = her herb green. Motion only on a change (`.pop`) and the due glow; all off under reduced motion.
- **Tested** (sandbox 8994, a made-up record "Ann Herbtest" as My profile, Gui Pi Tang 3 spoons twice a day Mon–Fri, dispensed Fri 23 Oct, 90 g): runs out Thu 5 Nov, "9 days left" (counted by hand too); typed 8:00 / 20:00 (saved, toast with Undo); a new script id kept the times; 8 am glowed gold at 10:23 and its tick turned it green (rail 1/2, "1 of 4" over the 7 days, Friday's two dashed), Undo, untick; the drawer ticks (2 of 2) and the grid repaint; ten blocks Mon–Fri on the week grid at 1280 (scaled to fit), today's tap = taken, gold when due; another day's card (8:00 pm · Dose 2 of 2 · Tue 27 Oct); phone 375: the page (no sideways scroll, times on one line after the fix), the chips above / below the day, a tap; Dispense opened her prescription on Dispense; ⋯ menu lists Herbs; the quiet time save (same field, still focused) then the repaint on leaving; Prescriptions search 3 → "Zed" 1 → 3. No console errors.
- **Not tested:** a dose inside a stack of 4+ (its row opens the same card through phC22PopHtml, code path only); her real data and her real prescription (which formula, whether she logs her own dispenses: with none logged the schedule uses her record's own script from today and shows no days left); two devices through the cloud row; the gold turning on by itself at the minute (the timer's code path only); a real phone's time picker.
- **Integration checked:** Herbs page, Me drawer, Appointments grid (week + phone day), a dose's card, the rail, the ⋯ menu, Dispense. Not shown elsewhere on purpose: the Mine hub's Week journal, Fasting, the Diet page.

## A smaller meal card (2026-10-26)
- **Her ask** (screenshot of the Break Fast card with + Food open, a sideways scrollbar along its bottom): "improve this display so it is more space saving".

  5. B: no "Planned" word; the Just today | Every <meal> bar sits under the time
  6. B: Had it and Edit on one row (Had it twice as wide)
  7. B: no count beside FOOD / DRINKS
  8. B: the cup only where food and drinks mix (the open list, the calendar, the Diet page), none under Drinks
- **Built** (`index.html`): `phMealListHtml` (chips `.ph-meal-it`, a dish's name a `data-meal-dish` button, `phMealNatDot` for its nature dot), `phMealListPickHtml` (`.ph-meal-lpk`: `.ph-meal-own` field + "+ New", `.ph-meal-chs` of `.ph-meal-ch` chips, `data-meal-n` on each for the narrowing), `phMealCardHtml` (no Planned label; Edit inside `.ph-meal-acts` while planned, its own row after Had it), the input handler narrows `[data-meal-n]`. CSS: the list block rewritten at TAPPABLE THINGS sizes (32px, 6px, 1px line, 13px); `.ph-meal-pick` gets `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)` (the snack picker too); `.ph-meal-acts .solid` grows 2; `.ph-meal-fastn + .ph-meal-bar` keeps its gap on a fast night. Removed as dead: the `.ph-meal-prow.on` / `.in` / `button.ph-meal-prow` rules (only the old list rows used them). `phMealDotIn` stays for the Diet page's lines.
- **Tested** (sandbox 8995, real clicks and the real handlers): closed 360px, open 506px (was ~510 / 736), scrollWidth = width (no sideways scroll); a dish chip adds it (solid, the list stays open, the toast's Undo); typing "coc" hides Meat Pie; "Toast" + Enter adds own:Toast and keeps the field focused; Done closes; ✕ removes Eating out; the latte's name opens its Drink editor and Save returns to the card; Every Breakfast makes the day's list her usual; Had it → "Meat Pie … + 2" with Undo, then Had it | Edit back on one row; her usual-meal sheet (no Skipped) and a patient's Diet sheet (Skipped, Same as usual) render the same chips; 360px phone sheet fits (336 = 336). **What it is:** `yangBody` in `PH_PP` (the mock's `YangPic` on PH_PP's own helpers): the Her build person (`anat`, now with `{ s, y0, h }`
so it can draw at 212/466 in a 300 x 252 frame) with three fires (Ming Men between the kidneys, the Spleen fire, the Heart fire), warmth
flowing up the trunk, out the arms and down the legs; Yang deficiency = the fires low and frosted, the flow short and slow, cold climbing
from the hands and feet, a cold belly and back, a pale face and lips, puffy ankles, clear urine falling, a slow heart that skips every

## Phone calendar: Google's spacing (2026-10-27)

Her ask: "improve my mobile ui calendar view, it feels too squished. use google calendar mobile as a guide for spacing.

`calendar-phone-spacing-mock-2026-10-27.html` (artifact T4BzKuua1H7xkV5mkjWLou, names fictional), her 9 picks then "Yes,
build it": 1 B one toolbar row · 2 A one date row · 3 A time column 64px, 11px hours · 4 A 3px gap · 5 A name first, 2
lines · 6 B text inset stays 7px · 7 A an hour stays 66px · 8 A no card · 9 A Saved pill shows 3 s.

Built, phone only (≤640px; the computer and tablet widths untouched):

  Me · 🔍. The date ▾ is a `.ph-atb-dd` whose menu holds the day counts (same `data-ph-apptcal-days` buttons), the
  Grid | List segment and Both clinics. 🔍 / ✕ are `data-ph-apptcal-srch="1|0"` (click handler beside the nav one):
  open adds `.srch` (the row shows only the search box, focused); ✕ clears `phApptCalQ` and repaints. `phApptCalSrch`
  keeps it open through the repaints typing makes.
- `phApptCalGridHtml`: `phone` / `one` (phone + 1 day). Gutter 64px on a phone. `one`: the head has no gutter cell; the
  day label (MON + date) sits in the time column, `.ph-apptcal-hd1` holds `phC22FoldRowHtml("before", …, bare=true)`
  (the one day's `.ph-c22-fd` cell, its ▴ inside when open), the fast chip and the CD chip (right). The separate "before"
  fold row is skipped; the trip row and the "after" row stay.
- CSS (PHONE REDESIGN block, "the calendar with Google Calendar's spacing"): wrap `margin: 0 -12px`, no border or
  radius, white; head / body / fold / trip rows `padding-right: 13px` (blocks end 16px from the edge), a `::after` on
  the grid carries the hour lines to the edge; hours 11px body font, `right: 12px`; the selected-day underline moved to
  `.hd1` (to the screen edge). Gap: blocks and her events get a transparent 1px top + right border with
  `background-clip: padding-box` on top of the grid's own 2px (the white seam ring stays, overlapping blocks still part).
  Name first: `.lg` blocks are a wrapping flex (name 100%, then the time, then the focus line with a "·" before it);
  sm / xs reorder their one line (name, then time; a narrow column drops the time whole: `:not(.lg) .r1` wraps at 18px);
  the herbs "!" moves to the block's top-right. Her events: name 14px / 600, time 12px; a tall one (time on its own
  line, `:has(> .tm)`) clamps the name to two lines. Selectors carry `.ph-apptcal-daycol` so they outrank the spacing
  audit's later rules.

  her pick's effect already holds and lengthening it to 3 s would cover the blocks longer. Told her; 3 s on her word.

## Came in for: edit in Details, any number of Mains, a sign on the bar (2026-10-27)
Her synth22 batch (closed with "fiinshed"): (1) the Compass header "From Baseline | Last visi" was cut; (2) "how to have more
than one main complaint"; (3) "how to choose if a sign can be tracked with the bar like complaints"; (4) "or select the sign as a
complaint too"; (5) "how to edit the chief complaint and complaints". One plan, mock `complaints-batch-mock-2026-10-27.html`
(artifact TEhyLsTvSsSYYgj491pf2J), her 8 picks, all the recommended ones, then "Yes, build it". Built in the order 1, 5, 2, 4, 3.
- **Header (item 1, no question):** the cut could not be made to happen at 360 / 1024 / 1160 / 1280 / 1440, so it is locked: a
  switch never shrinks (`.ph-cx-hd .ph-cx-sw { flex: none }`, nowrap words; `overflow: hidden` on a flex item let it shrink and
  clip), and From · the switches · Chart ▾ sit in one `.ph-cx-tools` group that moves down a line together.
- **Details on every row (Q4 Details ▾ in the panel, Q5 Name · How long · ★ Main · Remove):** `phCxCcFormHtml` for a typed
  complaint (the chief too), the pain's own form for a pain, `phCxSxTrackHtml` for a sign; the narrow card's drawer carries the
  same form. Name and How long save on change and update in place (`phCcWrite`; a tap that ends the typing is never lost); How
  long reads `phCcParseDatePrec` like the pain form. Remove on a secondary = `phCxRemoveSec` (Undo); on the chief =
  `phCxRemoveMain`: the next complaint (a Main one first) takes the slot with its own scores, notes, baseline and Goal (ccTrack
  `sec[id]` moves to `main`), none left = the slot empties and Came in for reads the pain map / plan again; Undo restores both
  records.
- **Any number of Mains (Q1 any number, Q3 each Main first in its own group, groups with a Main first):** `star` on every item
  (`phCxItems`): the chief's is `!c.mainOff`, a secondary's `s.main`, a pain's `p.main` (with no pain starred, the pain that
  carries a hidden chief shows Main by `st.chiefStar`). `main` still means the chief's slot (key, family, Goal), which never
  moves, so every complaint keeps its own scores. `phCxStarToggle` is the one switch (the panel, the drawer, the pain form, the
  Musculoskeletal pain table through `phPmSetMain`, which no longer clears the other pains or overwrites a typed chief); one
  complaint always stays Main ("One complaint stays Main"). The old table's ★ (`phCcSecPromote`) is the same switch now: its
  2026-10-15 swap left the score history with the slot, not the complaint (fixed on the way).
- **One-line places (Q2 every Main joined):** `phCxMainsOf` / `phCxCcMulti` / `phCxAlsoOf`; with more than one Main (or a Main
  that is not the chief) the Care Plan's Came in for row reads "★ Poor sleep + Headaches · Bloating", Aim "poor sleep and
  headaches", Watch a "main" line per Main, `phCcFillAim` addresses every Main; with one Main they read exactly as before. Copy
  notes has no Main line (it lists every score), so nothing changed there. The File search tags a Main secondary "Main".
- **A sign's two doors (Q6 both, Q7 stays in its Signs line, Q8 stays ticked + Sign tag):** Track with Better · Same · Worse |
  Bar 0–10 (`phCxSxTrack`, `rec.ccTrack.sxBar[signKey] = { id, at }`, back = `{ id, off }` so its bar scores return with it);
  on the bar it is scored like a complaint under `s:<id>` (its first bar score is its baseline), drawn after its group's
  complaints with its Sign tag (`.sxbar`), its earlier ratings under "Before" in Details, its pills row hidden (`phCxSignList`);
  no Goal (the Care Plan Goal skips it), never a pain (`phCxPainDup`). Make it a complaint (`phCxSignToComplaint`, now in
  Details too) keeps a bar sign's id and scores, leaves the Fang Bing Ren tick, and the complaint wears a small Sign tag;
  Remove drops the complaint and the sign row comes back.

Her words: "include a other option to add unusual conditions in medical history". Mock `hx-other-mock-2026-10-27.html`
(Artifact "History Other Condition"), her 4 picks, all A, then "Yes, build it". Built: `shots/hx-other-built-desktop-2026-10-27.png`,

**Her picks:** 1 A "+ Other condition" at the end of General health: type, Add, it is its own Yes row (Added tag, ✕ removes it) with
its note; 2 A the same at the end of Family history (blood relatives); 3 A the patient's history link gets "+ Something else" and it
arrives as an Added Yes row with the patient's words, tagged Form; 4 A a typed condition shows everywhere a Yes shows.
**Code (index.html):** `phHxOtherItems` (the typed rows that are Yes, oldest first), `phHxWithOther` (puts them where their group
ends; `phHxApplicableItems` and the figure's `phHxItems` read it), `phHxOtherFind` (a list row of the same words and kind, else a
typed row of that name), `phHxOtherPut` (Yes on that row, making the typed row when there is none), `phHxOtherFromForm`,
`phHxOtherRemove` (returns the Undo), `phHxOtherRowHtml` / `phHxOtherAddHtml` / `phHxOtherCommit` beside `phHxBodyHtml`; taps
`data-hx-oadd` / `data-hx-ook` / `data-hx-orm` before `data-hx-set`; Enter / Esc on `data-hx-oin` (a window capture listener, so
Esc closes the box and not the history sheet); view state `presHxOtherAdd`. CSS `.ph-hx-orow`, `.ph-hx-otag`, `.ph-hx-orm`,
`.ph-hx-oadd`, `.ph-hx-oadd-box`, `.ph-hx-ook` (beside the group-note rules). The herb caution (`phClinicalFlag`) matches a typed
condition on its own words (4 letters or more), own or family, as the list's family rows already do.
**The link:** intake.html `otherRows` / `otherAddRow` / `otherRenderRows` (Condition + Details, ×), sent as `history.others = [{ n,
f: 1 = family, note }]` (20 at most; a plain key on the jsonb blob, no SQL); a resend brings the rows back with their details. The
app sends `prefill.others` = the conditions the PATIENT wrote before (`src: "form"`, names only); her own typed conditions and every
note stay in the app. Review: a new one = "X: Yes (added by the patient) · details"; one on file as a Yes only brings details its
note lacks; a list row of the same words answered No or Don't know is a Keep / Use new choice (key `other-<i>`: the choice buttons
split their key on ":"); the same condition twice on one form is listed once.

## The freeze on load (2026-10-27)
Her report: "the app has been freezing and taking a long time to load on the desktop - find out how to resolve this".
- **Seen:** her LCM window (the installed app, Chrome) sat on "Loading your pharmacy..." under Chrome's "Page Unresponsive";
  its page process used a whole core and grew 660 → 776 MB. The live build in a Chrome tab froze the same way. The sandbox
  (made-up data) started in 2 s, so it was her records.
- **How it was found (read-only, reusable for the next freeze):**
  - Host: a same-site page outside every app's scope with no security rule (the C6 icon,
    `b00k33.github.io/c6-jingfang/assets/favicon-32.png`). Any `/lcm-pharmacy/` address opens in her app window instead,
    and GitHub's 404 page blocks scripts.
  - The probe: her installed build's text (from the `lcm-` cache) written into a frame on that page. Every save went to a
    memory copy, IndexedDB and cache writes were no-ops, sending was blocked, sync was off, the worker was not registered.
  - Every loop head and function entry was counted. Every 300 ms a short progress note (counts and the call chain, no
    records) was written to `zzprobe-trail`, read after the frozen tab was ended, then removed.
  - Scripts: scratchpad build9 probe2.js to probe4.js.
- **Cause:** a circle among the written-from-the-record summaries:
  - The booking brief asks the Care Plan for its goal (`phApptBrief` → `phTpAutoGoal`, 10-10).
  - The goal reads the complaints (`phCxItems` → `phCcRibItems` → `phCcAuto`, 10-21).
  - The complaints read each open plan's pain map (`phPmList`).
  - A plan with no saved pain map asks the booking brief for its complaint (`phPmComplaint` → `phApptBrief`), and around
    again.
  - Each overflow was caught (`try`/`catch` in `run` and `phCcAuto`) and the next plan tried, so it branched once per open
    plan. With her records (670 patients, 99 with plans, about 800 prescriptions) a turn outlasted the 1.5 s memo window,
    the memo emptied, and it never settled. On smaller data it settled, slowly.

## Care Plan part 2, step 4: course length from the patient (2026-10-27)

Her pick 5 ("How long" chips at the door; a longer history adds visits to the first two phases), mock

- **One fact:** the chips are the main concern's own How long (`complaint.since`, the Came in for row's box), not a second
  answer. `phCcLenBand(since)` = the band by whole months back: under 2 = Weeks, under 6 = Months, under 12 = 6–12 months, under
  36 = 1–3 years, else Longer. A chip writes 3 weeks / 3 months / 9 months / 2 years / 5 years back as a "~" worked-out date
  (`phCcMainSinceSet(iso, false, true)`, which repaints Came in for and the door); the chip of the band her own date is already
  in does nothing, so a typed date is never overwritten by its own band. The Weeks / Months line (2 months) is mine; both add 0.
- **The door** (`phTpDoorStartHtml`, under Came in for): "How long" + the five chips (32 px, the lit one solid), then Start, now
  "Course · Low back pain · 3 phases · 9 visits" (the course's planned visits with the band's extra).
- **The course** (`phTpCourseLenApply`): when a course starts (`presTpInlineCreate`: the door and "+ New"; `phTpCreate`) or is
  swapped (Change course → Swap the phases), the band adds visits to phase 1 / phase 2: 6–12 months +1 / 0, 1–3 years +1 / +1,
  Longer +2 / +2 (the mock's table: Low back pain 7 → 8 → 9 → 11). Only a phase that has a count gets more. Cycle courses
  (`PH_TP_CYCLE_TEMPLATES`) keep theirs: they follow the calendar. Written once into `phase.sessions`, hers to change after.

  14 logged visits; 15 of 40 course plans past their phase's planned visits and still in it. Reading the code: bookings
  already counted (`phTpPhaseSessionDates`, `phTpPhaseVisitStats`); the move lived only in the session-log save hook.
- **The card** (`phTpPrvCtx` / `phTpPrvHtml`): shows when the visits before today + today reach the planned count, whether or
  not today is logged (part 2 hid it once today was logged, because the log carried out the pick). Nothing is pre-picked (part
  2 had Move solid). `ctx.last` = the date of the planned-th visit (today when it is today's).
- **The tap** (`phTpPrvDo`, the click handler on `data-tp-prv-pick`): Stay = `ph.sessions` + half again, review "Staying 2 more
  visits"; Move = `phTpPhaseStatusData(plan, next, "current")`, review "Moved to Subacute", and when the planned-th visit was
  before today the old phase's `doneKey` = that day and the next phase's `sinceKey` = the day after (so the visits since count
  for the next phase); Close (last phase) = plan done, phase `doneKey` today. Each review carries `prv.undo` ({v, sessions}).
  Then `savePharmacy()` + `renderPresPanel()` (keeps the scroll).
- **Undo** (`data-tp-prv-undo`, `phTpPrvUndo`): removes that review; Stay puts the old count back; Move makes the old phase
  current again (`phTpPhaseStatusData`, later phases upcoming); Close reopens the plan and the phase.
- **Logging a visit** (the `data-pres-acu-log` save) no longer moves the plan, writes a review or sets `phTpAutoAdv`; the
  card stays until her tap. The Treatment tab banner code for `phTpAutoAdv` is left in place, unreached.

## Care Plan part 3, step 5: the cycle review (2026-10-27)

Her pick 5 and her ask28 answer "At her next booking" (not when the period is logged). Mock section 5. Measured: 26 cycle plans
(22 with an LMP, 8 with cycle day logs); 9 of 12 had a period in the last 90 days. Already there: the cycle history table
(`phCycleHistoryHtml`: starts from `phBbtCycleStarts`, flow / pain from `rec.cycleLog`).

- **`phCycRvModel(rec, plan)`**: an active cycle-template plan with three or more starts. `st[k]` is the period that began the
  cycle she is in; the cycle that just ended is `st[k-1]`..`st[k]`, the one before `st[k-2]`..`st[k-1]`. Each: length in
  days, the period's `flowIntensity` and `pain` from its `cycleLog` entry, `clot` = the most clots on its days
  (`phCycClots` of `rec.cycleSigns[d]`: many 3, large 2, small 1).

  `.tg` tags of the review card.

  Choline from USDA where it has the same food (chips, fries, pot pies, whole milk), otherwise not counted. Build source:
  scratchpad session 4f11f526 `ausnut/` (rows.pl, spec.txt → rows.js).

  Food Facts' search refuses a web page (no CORS) and its bulk search returned 503. So the app carries a copy: `foods-au.json`,
  from Open Food Facts' CSV export (818 MB compressed, streamed, never stored; export of 2026-10-27, read 2026-10-28). 2,117,569
  products read → 18,413 Australian (country tag or a 930–939 barcode) with protein, carbs and fat → **17,772 kept** (415 with
  energy more than 40% off its own macros dropped, 52 impossible; repeats of one name + energy merged, the most scanned kept; a
  record with no energy gets it from its macros, 17 · 17 · 37 · 8 kJ/g). Shops from the record's stores and brands: Woolworths
  ~4,770, Coles ~3,450, Aldi ~1,120 (an Aldi own brand or an Aldi barcode 40886 / 40887 / 40614 counts), IGA 43, Costco 29.
  1.8 MB, ~0.6 MB as Pages sends it. Row: `[code, name (brand first), pack, serve g/ml, drink, kJ, P, C, F, fibre, sugar, sodium
  mg, scans, {minerals / vitamins the label gives}, shops]` per 100 g (100 ml for a drink). Build source: `off/au.pl` (the
  stream filter), `off/json.pl` (tidy, check, shops), `off/sf.js` + `off/food.pl` (the code; food.pl replays every edit onto a
  HEAD copy: `perl food.pl index.html rows.js sf.js 20261028`).
- **How it works (`phSf*`, "SHOP FOODS" after `PH_TB_TOP`):** the first time she types in a meal's add list, `phSfLoad` fetches
  `PH_SF_URL` (the worker then keeps it, cache-first, for offline). `phSfHtml` puts a **Shops** block under her own foods while
  she searches (heading "Shops · Open Food Facts", "· loading", "· offline"), up to 12 rows: every typed word whole, the last one
  a start ("meat" no longer finds Meatless); her shops' products and Australian barcodes first, then a name that starts with her
  first word, then the most scanned. A tap (`data-meal-sf`, then the usual `data-meal-tog`) keeps the product in her Me row
  `d.sfood["sh_<code>"]` (`phSfEnsure`; merged entry by entry like dishes / meals / shop) and registers it into `PH_FOOD` as group
  "sh" "From the shops" (`phSfReg`, also on every Me read / write and once after the food constants), at its label serve.
  Numbers not on the label are "not counted". Credit under Targets: AUSNUT 2023 (FSANZ) · shop products: Open Food Facts (ODbL).
  `.github/workflows/pages.yml` now copies foods-au.json (it is fetched, not linked).
- **Refreshing the shop file:** re-run the stream (`curl -sL https://static.openfoodfacts.org/data/en.openfoodfacts.org.products.csv.gz
  | gzip -dc | perl au.pl > au.tsv`, ~15 min), `perl json.pl au.tsv foods-au.json <date>`, and bump `PH_SF_URL`'s `?d=` so the

## Meals macros against goal (2026-10-28)

Her ask, with a screenshot of her Meals week planner: "show the macros consumption vs goal - show 3 mocks". Mock
`meals-macros-mock-2026-10-28.html` (published as an artifact: A in the table, B today on top, C a week chart). Her picks: **A + B
together**; all four numbers (kJ, protein, carbs, fat); goals = **kJ + a split** with her own grams winning (protein: her 50 g wins);
over the goal = **deep for all four**, under 60% = amber; the rings **under the clock bar**; days to come **as planned, pale**; "Yes,
build it". Mid-build, her word: **"set carbs to 50g a day"**.

- **Goals** (`phDietGoal`): `PH_DIET_GOAL0.cb = 50` (her word; Targets tags it "yours"); fat = her own, else (kJ − 17 × protein − 17
  × carbs) / 37 (FSANZ energy factors), only while she has a kJ goal (Targets tags it "from kJ"). With protein and carbs both fixed
  in grams the split leaves fat as the rest, so no % fields were built. kJ has no goal until she types one. Clearing fat's box
  says "Fat · the rest of your kJ".
- **Today's rings** (`phMacRingsHtml`, added to `fbar` in `phMplHtml`): "Today · Wed 28" + had / planned key, four rings (solid =
  had via `phDietMyDay`, pale = with what is planned via `phMplPlanSum`), the %, the amount, "of" + the goal as a 26px tinted field
  (`.gf.field-bare`, the app's opt-out from the field rule; `data-diet-goal` so the same change handler and `phDietGoalSet` save it),
  "n to go" / "n over" / "✓ goal". The focus after a save comes back to the box she moved to, in the rings or in Targets
  (`phDietTgFocus` is now a selector). On a phone the rings are the day it shows (‹ ›), four across 360px.
- **The Macros row** (`phMacCellHtml`, a `<tr class="mac">` before More on the computer's week table): kJ / P / C / F, each a short
  bar (solid had, pale the rest of the plan) and its number (`data-roll`, so it counts as a meal is had: the More button's kJ roll
  moved here). A day to come is pale; a plan over its goal shows a deep number. The table's key gained had / under 60% / over goal /
  planned.
- **Colours** (`phMacOne`): over the goal = `--ph-herb-deep`; under 60% = `--ph-low`, on today only when what is planned also falls
  short (the morning would otherwise always read amber). Tokens `--ph-mac-*` on `.ph-mpl`, so her gynae page draws them crimson.
- **More**: its button shows the day's glasses only (its kJ is on the Macros row and the rings); the row's label reads "water".
- **Tested** (sandbox, made-up "Zoe Mock" with a fertility case, a week of meals, goal 7,500 kJ): rings and row at 1280 and 360

  breakfast strips, cooked", per 100 g: 1,879 kJ, protein 31.3 g, carbs 1.4 g, fat 34.4 g, sodium 2,253 mg, choline 119.2 mg, B12
  3.45 µg; no iodine given (not counted). The strip is USDA's own portion (3 slices = 34 g). New unit plural "strips"
  (`PH_FOOD_UNITS`). Search words: beef strips, breakfast strips.

  Japan 2020, 8th edition (MEXT) 16035 "Matcha", per 100 g: 984 kJ, protein 29.6 g, carbs 1.6 g (its available carbohydrate, as
  AFCD's carbs are), fat 5.3 g, fibre 38.5 g, iron 17 mg, calcium 420 mg, vitamin C 60 mg, folate 1,200 µg; no sugars, choline,
  iodine or omega-3 given (not counted). Search words: green tea powder, powdered green tea.
